subject: Biology
title: DNA Fingerprinting
description: Alec Jeffreys. Uses Satellite DNA (VNTRs - Variable Number Tandem Repeats). Steps: Isolation -> Digestion -> Electrophoresis -> Blotting -> Probe Hybridization.
visual_data:
VNTR: Mini-satellite DNA
Sensitivity: PCR increases sample
Blotting: Southern Blot (Nitrocellulose)

subject: Biology
title: Lac Operon Regulation
description: Jacob & Monod. Polycistronic structural gene (z, y, a). Regulated by Repressor protein (from i gene). Lactose is Inducer.

subject: Biology
title: Genetic Code Properties
description: Triplet code (61 codons for AA, 3 Stop). Universal (AUG is Start/Met). Degenerate (One AA has multiple codons). Unambiguous.
visual_data:
AUG: Start Codon (Methionine)
UAA, UAG, UGA: Stop Codons
Degenerate: wobble hypothesis

subject: Biology
title: Human Genome Project
description: Completed 2003. 3 x 10^9 base pairs. 20,000-25,000 genes. Less than 2% codes for proteins. Chromosome 1 has most genes (2968), Y has fewest (231).
visual_data: \begin{aligned} 3.3 \times 10^9 \text{ bp (Haploid)} \\ 99.9\% \text{ Nucleotides same in all humans} \end{aligned}

subject: Biology
title: Types of RNA
description: rRNA is most abundant (80%). 23S rRNA acts as Ribozyme (Peptide bond formation). mRNA carries codon info.
derivation: Central Dogma flow facilitators.

subject: Biology
title: Nucleosome Model
visual_data: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 150' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><circle cx='100' cy='80' r='40' fill='#E5E7EB' stroke='#9CA3AF'/><text x='100' y='85' text-anchor='middle' font-size='10'>Histone Octamer</text><path d='M40,120 Q100,20 160,120' fill='none' stroke='#EF4444' stroke-width='4'/><text x='170' y='130' font-size='10' fill='#EF4444'>DNA (200 bp)</text><rect x='140' y='50' width='10' height='20' fill='#3B82F6'/><text x='160' y='60' font-size='10' fill='#3B82F6'>H1</text></svg>
description: DNA packaging. Negatively charged DNA wrapped around Positively charged Histone Octamer (H2A, H2B, H3, H4 x2). H1 is linker histone.
derivation: Beads-on-string structure.

subject: Biology
title: Post-Transcriptional Modifications
description: Eukaryotes only. hnRNA -> Capping (5' mGPPP) + Tailing (3' Poly-A) + Splicing (Introns removed, Exons joined) -> mRNA.

subject: Biology
title: DNA vs RNA Stability
description: DNA (Deoxyribose) lacks 2'-OH -> More stable, chemically less reactive. RNA (Ribose) has 2'-OH -> Labile, catalytic (Ribozyme).
visual_data:
DNA: Genetic material (Storage)
RNA: Transmission of information / Catalysis

subject: Biology
title: Chargaff's Rule
description: Base equivalence in double-stranded DNA (purines = pyrimidines). \(A\)=adenine, \(T\)=thymine, \(G\)=guanine, \(C\)=cytosine; ratio \((A+T)/(G+C)\) is species-specific.

subject: Biology
title: Base Pair Hydrogen Bonds
visual_data: A = T \;(\text{2 H-bonds}) \\ G \equiv C \;(\text{3 H-bonds})
description: Number of hydrogen bonds per base pair; G-C richer DNA is more thermostable. Adenine pairs with Thymine via 2 bonds, Guanine with Cytosine via 3.

subject: Biology
title: B-DNA Helix Dimensions
description: Watson-Crick B-form DNA geometry (most asked NEET numbers). Pitch = length of one full helical turn; 10 base pairs stacked per turn; each pair rises \(0.34\,nm\).

subject: Biology
title: Number of Codons
description: Total triplet codons from 4 bases taken 3 at a time. 61 code for amino acids (sense), 3 are stop codons; AUG codes Met and acts as start.

subject: Biology
title: Amino Acids Coded
description: Standard number of amino acids specified by the genetic code; degeneracy means multiple codons per amino acid. 20 amino acids encoded by 61 sense codons.

subject: Biology
title: DNA Packaging Ratio
description: Nucleosome organization of chromatin. ~200 bp DNA associates with one nucleosome; core wraps ~146 bp in 1.75 turns around 8 histones (octamer); H1 is the linker.

subject: Biology
title: Meselson-Stahl Experiment
description: Proof of semiconservative DNA replication using N-isotope density-gradient (CsCl) centrifugation. Generation 1 = all hybrid (\(^{15}N/^{14}N\)); Generation 2 = 50% hybrid, 50% light.

subject: Biology
title: Hershey-Chase Labels
description: Radioactive labels proving DNA (not protein) is the genetic material in bacteriophages. Phosphorus-32 tags DNA backbone; Sulphur-35 tags protein coat (DNA lacks S, protein lacks P).

subject: Biology
title: Human Genome Project Genes
description: Key HGP gene-count statistics. Human genome has far fewer genes than expected; average gene ~3000 bp; chromosome 1 has most genes, Y the fewest.

subject: Biology
title: Lac Operon Genes
description: Structural genes of the lac operon (polycistronic) and regulator. \(z\)=breaks lactose into glucose+galactose, \(y\)=transports lactose, \(a\)=transacetylase; \(i\) gene makes repressor.

subject: Biology
title: RNA Polymerases (Eukaryote)
visual_data: \begin{aligned} \text{RNA Pol I} &\rightarrow rRNA\,(28S,18S,5.8S) \\ \text{RNA Pol II} &\rightarrow hnRNA\,(\text{mRNA precursor}) \\ \text{RNA Pol III} &\rightarrow tRNA,\,5S\,rRNA,\,snRNA \end{aligned}
description: Three eukaryotic RNA polymerases and their transcripts. Pol I = ribosomal RNAs, Pol II = heterogeneous nuclear RNA (mRNA precursor), Pol III = transfer/small RNAs.

subject: Biology
title: Mitochondria Structure
description: Double-membrane bound organelle. Inner membrane folds into Cristae to increase surface area for ATP production (Oxidative Phosphorylation).

title: Ribosome Subunits
description: Prokaryotes (70S = 50S + 30S). Eukaryotes (80S = 60S + 40S). 'S' is Svedberg Unit (Sedimentation coefficient).

title: Chloroplast Structure
description: Double membrane. Thylakoids (Light Reaction). Stroma (Dark Reaction). Grana (Stacks of Thylakoids). Contains 70S Ribosomes & circular DNA.

subject: Biology
title: Ribosome Types
description: Protein factories. Composed of rRNA and proteins. Prokaryotic (70S) and Eukaryotic (80S). 'S' = Svedberg Unit.

subject: Biology
title: Fluid Mosaic Model
visual_data: <svg viewBox='0 0 300 100' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='0' y='30' width='300' height='40' fill='#F3F4F6'/><circle cx='20' cy='30' r='5' fill='#3B82F6'/><line x1='20' y1='30' x2='20' y2='50' stroke='#000'/><circle cx='20' cy='70' r='5' fill='#3B82F6'/><line x1='20' y1='70' x2='20' y2='50' stroke='#000'/><text x='20' y='15' font-size='8'>Polar Head</text><ellipse cx='80' cy='50' rx='15' ry='30' fill='#F59E0B'/><text x='80' y='90' font-size='8'>Integral Protein</text><circle cx='140' cy='25' r='10' fill='#10B981'/><text x='140' y='10' font-size='8'>Peripheral</text><path d='M200,30 L210,10 L220,30' fill='none' stroke='#000'/><text x='230' y='20' font-size='8'>Sugar Chain</text></svg>

derivation: Quasi-fluid nature enables cell growth, secretion, endocytosis.

title: Cilia/Flagella Structure
description: 9+2 Arrangement of microtubules in axoneme. 9 peripheral doublets + 2 central singlets. Basal body has 9+0 arrangement.

subject: Biology
title: Nucleus Structure
description: Double membrane (Nuclear envelope) with pores. Nucleoplasm contains Chromatin (DNA+Histones) and Nucleolus (rRNA synthesis site).
visual_data:
Heterochromatin: Densely packed, Transcriptionally inactive
Euchromatin: Loosely packed, Active

subject: Biology
title: Cytoskeleton
description: Network of filamentous proteinaceous structures. Microtubules (Tubulin), Microfilaments (Actin). Functions: Support, Motility, Shape maintenance.
visual_data:
Microtubules: Spindle fibers, Cilia, Flagella
Microfilaments: Muscle contraction, Pseudopodia

subject: Biology
title: Prokaryotic Envelope
description: 3 Layers: Glycocalyx (Slime layer/Capsule), Cell Wall (Peptidoglycan), Plasma Membrane (Mesosomes - respiration).

title: Golgi Apparatus
description: Camillo Golgi. Cis face (forming) and Trans face (maturing). Functions: Packaging, Modification (Glycosylation - Glycoproteins/Glycolipids).

subject: Biology
title: Endomembrane System
description: Functionally coordinated organelles. ER (Synthesis) -> Golgi (Packaging) -> Lysosome (Digestion) -> Vacuole (Storage).

subject: Biology
title: Cell Theory Exception
visual_data: \text{Omnis cellula-e cellula} \\ \text{(All cells from pre-existing cells)} \\ \text{Exception: Viruses, Viroids, Prions}
description: Cell theory (Schleiden, Schwann; modified by Virchow) and its non-cellular exceptions for NEET assertion-reason.

subject: Biology
title: Smallest & Largest Cell
visual_data: \text{Smallest: PPLO/Mycoplasma} \approx 0.3\,\mu m \\ \text{Largest cell: Ostrich egg} \\ \text{Longest: Nerve cell}
description: Standard size landmarks frequently asked in NEET. \(\mu m\)=micrometre. RBC \(\approx 7\,\mu m\); bacteria \(1\!-\!2\,\mu m\).

subject: Biology
title: Prokaryote vs Eukaryote Size
description: Typical diameter range distinguishing the two cell types. \(\mu m\)=micrometre (\(10^{-6}\) m).

subject: Biology
title: Bacterial Ribosome (70S)
description: Prokaryotic ribosome composition and rRNA constituents. S=Svedberg sedimentation unit (non-additive). Site of protein synthesis; polysome when multiple on one mRNA.

subject: Biology
title: Eukaryotic 80S rRNA
description: Eukaryotic cytoplasmic ribosome rRNA components. S=Svedberg unit. Note organelle (mito/chloroplast) ribosomes are 70S.

subject: Biology
title: Centriole Microtubule Array
description: Centriole/basal body microtubule arrangement. Each of 9 peripheral fibrils is a triplet; hub-and-spoke cartwheel; forms basal body of cilia/flagella.

subject: Biology
title: Cilia/Flagella Axoneme
description: Axoneme microtubule pattern of cilia and eukaryotic flagella. Peripheral pairs linked to central by radial spokes; central sheath connects the doublet.

subject: Biology
title: Singer-Nicolson Model Year
description: Year and proposers of the accepted membrane model; quasi-fluid lipid bilayer allows lateral movement. Lipids arranged with polar heads out, hydrophobic tails in.

subject: Biology
title: Nuclear Pore & Genome
description: Human somatic chromosome number and the bilayer nuclear envelope perforated by nuclear pores for nucleocytoplasmic exchange. \(2n\)=diploid number.

subject: Biology
title: Mycoplasma Distinction
visual_data: \text{Smallest living cell} \\ \text{No cell wall} \\ d \approx 0.3\,\mu m
description: Mycoplasma (PPLO) key recall facts: smallest free-living cell, wall-less, pleomorphic. \(d\)=diameter. Can survive without oxygen.

subject: Biology
title: Bacterial Cell Wall (Gram)
visual_data: \text{Gram +ve: thick peptidoglycan, retains stain} \\ \text{Gram -ve: thin wall + outer membrane}
description: Gram staining basis (Christian Gram) distinguishing bacterial wall types; peptidoglycan = murein. Determines stain retention (purple vs pink).

subject: Biology
title: Bacterial Flagellum Parts
description: Three structural components of a bacterial flagellum; structurally distinct from eukaryotic 9+2 flagellum (no microtubules).

subject: Biology
title: Mesosome Function
description: Mesosome = extension of plasma membrane in prokaryotes aiding wall formation, DNA replication, respiration and secretion (analogue of organelles).

subject: Biology
title: Microbody / Lysosome Enzymes
description: Lysosomes (rich in acid hydrolases, optimally active at acidic pH) digest carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids; formed by Golgi.

subject: Biology
title: Cell Cycle Phases
description: Interphase occupies 95% of the duration (G1, S, G2). M-Phase (Mitosis) is the actual division phase.

subject: Biology
title: Prophase I Stages
description: Leptotene (Condensation), Zygotene (Synapsis/Bivalent), Pachytene (Crossing Over/Recombination), Diplotene (Chiasmata), Diakinesis (Terminalization).
visual_data:
LZPDD Mnemonic:
Lazy (Leptotene)
Zebra (Zygotene)
Pushes (Pachytene)
Dumb (Diplotene)
Donkey (Diakinesis)

subject: Biology
title: Mitosis Stages
description: Prophase (Condensation). Metaphase (Equatorial Plate). Anaphase (Centromere splits, Chromatids move). Telophase (Decondensation).

subject: Biology
title: Cell Cycle Checkpoints
description: Control mechanisms. G1/S (Restriction Point) - checks DNA damage. G2/M - checks DNA replication. M (Spindle) - checks chromosome attachment.
visual_data:
G1/S: Decision to divide (Start)
G2/M: DNA Replication complete?
M: Metaphase alignment correct?

subject: Biology
title: Anaphase I vs Anaphase II
description: Anaphase I: Homologous chromosomes separate (Segregation), Centromere does NOT split. Anaphase II: Centromere splits, Sister chromatids separate.

title: Crossing Over

description: Exchange of genetic material between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes. Enzyme: Recombinase. Occurs in Pachytene.
derivation: Leads to genetic variation.

subject: Biology
title: Significance of Meiosis
description: 1. Conservation of chromosome number across generations (2n -> n). 2. Genetic variability (Crossing over). 3. Evolution.

subject: Biology
title: Meiosis II (Equational)
description: Resembles Mitosis. Prophase II -> Metaphase II (Chromosomes align) -> Anaphase II (Centromere splits) -> Telophase II (4 Haploid cells).
visual_data: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 100' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><circle cx='50' cy='50' r='40' fill='none' stroke='#000'/><line x1='50' y1='20' x2='50' y2='80' stroke='#EF4444' stroke-width='2'/><text x='50' y='95' text-anchor='middle' font-size='8'>Metaphase II</text><path d='M120,50 L140,50' stroke='#000' marker-end='url(#arrow)'/><circle cx='180' cy='30' r='15' fill='none' stroke='#000'/><circle cx='180' cy='70' r='15' fill='none' stroke='#000'/><text x='180' y='95' text-anchor='middle' font-size='8'>4 Daughter Cells</text></svg>

subject: Biology
title: Cell Cycle Duration (Human)
description: Standard duration of a typical human cell cycle. Interphase occupies ~95% of the cycle, M phase ~1 hr.

subject: Biology
title: DNA Content Through Cell Cycle
description: DNA amount (C-value) doubles in S phase, halves at mitosis end. Ploidy (2n) stays constant in mitosis even though DNA changes 2C to 4C.

subject: Biology
title: Mitosis Output
description: One diploid parent yields two genetically identical diploid daughter cells; chromosome number conserved.

subject: Biology
title: Number of Chiasmata
description: Minimum one crossover (chiasma) per homologous pair ensures proper segregation. A bivalent = 2 homologues = 4 chromatids (tetrad).

subject: Biology
title: Bivalents in Meiosis I
description: Number of synapsed homologous pairs (bivalents) seen at metaphase I equals haploid number. For humans n=23 bivalents.

subject: Biology
title: Genetic Variation Combinations
description: Number of chromosomally distinct gametes from independent assortment, where \(n\)=haploid number. Human \(2^{23}\). (Excludes crossing-over variation.)

subject: Biology
title: Human Chromosome Number
description: Diploid (somatic) and haploid (gamete) chromosome numbers in humans. \(2n\)=diploid, \(n\)=haploid.

subject: Biology
title: G0 (Quiescent) Phase
description: Cells that do not divide further leave the cycle at G1 entering the inactive (quiescent) G0 stage.

subject: Biology
title: S Phase: DNA vs Centriole
description: In S phase DNA doubles and the centriole duplicates in cytoplasm, but chromosome number (ploidy) is unchanged.

subject: Biology
title: Meiosis: Two Divisions
description: Single round of DNA replication followed by two sequential divisions. Meiosis I halves chromosome number; Meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

subject: Biology
title: Human Heart Flow
description: Double circulation pathway: Right Atrium -> Right Ventricle -> Lungs (Pulmonary) -> Left Atrium -> Left Ventricle -> Body (Systemic).

subject: Biology
title: Electrocardiogram (ECG)
description: P-Wave (Atrial Depolarization). QRS Complex (Ventricular Depolarization). T-Wave (Ventricular Repolarization). Count QRS to get Heart Rate.

subject: Biology
title: Blood Group Compatibility
description: Antigens on RBC surface. Antibodies in Plasma. O- is Universal Donor (No antigens). AB+ is Universal Recipient (No antibodies).

subject: Biology
title: Coagulation Cascade
description: Cascade mechanism. Calcium ions ($Ca^{++}$) play a crucial role in both steps. Vitamin K required for Prothrombin synthesis.
derivation: Injury $\to$ Thromboplastin $\to$ Thrombokinase enzyme complex.

subject: Biology
title: Cardiac Cycle (0.8s)
description: Sequence of events in one heartbeat. Atrial Systole (0.1s) -> Ventricular Systole (0.3s) -> Joint Diastole (0.4s). Stroke Volume = 70ml.
visual_data: \text{Lub} \to \text{Closure of AV valves (Vent. Systole)} \\ \text{Dub} \to \text{Closure of Semilunar valves (Vent. Diastole)}

subject: Biology
title: Lymphatic System
description: Tissue fluid (Interstitial fluid). Similar to plasma but fewer proteins. Carries fats (Lacteals in villi) and lymphocytes (Immunity). Drains back to veins.

subject: Biology
title: Circulatory Disorders
description: Hypertension (>140/90). CAD (Atherosclerosis - Ca/Fat deposits in arteries). Angina (Chest pain - low O2). Heart Failure (Pumping failure).
visual_data:
Cardiac Arrest: Heart stops beating
Heart Attack: Muscle damage due to no blood supply

subject: Biology
title: Cardiac Output
description: Volume of blood pumped by each ventricle per minute. \(CO\)=cardiac output, \(SV\)=stroke volume (~70 mL), \(HR\)=heart rate (~72 beats/min). Normal CO \(\approx\) 5 L/min.

subject: Biology
title: Blood Composition
description: Proportion of fluid matrix vs cells in blood. Plasma is ~55% by volume, formed elements (RBC, WBC, platelets) ~45%. Plasma itself is ~90-92% water and 6-8% proteins.

subject: Biology
title: Plasma Proteins
description: Major plasma proteins by abundance. Albumin (osmotic balance), globulins (immunity/antibodies), fibrinogen (clotting). Total plasma protein ~7 g/dL.

subject: Biology
title: RBC Count
description: Normal erythrocyte (red blood cell) count in a healthy adult. ~5 to 5.5 million RBCs per cubic mm of blood. Formed in red bone marrow.

subject: Biology
title: RBC Lifespan
description: Average circulating life of a red blood cell before destruction in spleen ('graveyard of RBCs') and liver. Enucleate biconcave cells.

subject: Biology
title: WBC Differential (%)
description: Relative abundance of WBC types (mnemonic 'Never Let Monkeys Eat Bananas', most to least). Neutrophils most abundant; basophils rarest.

subject: Biology
title: Platelet Count
description: Normal thrombocyte count. ~1.5 to 3.5 lakh per cubic mm. Cell fragments from megakaryocytes; aid blood clotting. Low count = clotting disorders.

subject: Biology
title: Pacemaker (SAN) Rate
description: Sino-atrial node, the natural pacemaker, generates the highest impulse frequency, setting heart rate ~72/min. Sequence: SAN \(\rightarrow\) AVN \(\rightarrow\) Bundle of His \(\rightarrow\) Purkinje fibres.

subject: Biology
title: Cardiac Cycle Subdivisions
description: Time split within one 0.8 s cardiac cycle (HR 72/min). Atrial systole 0.1 s, ventricular systole 0.3 s, complete cardiac diastole 0.4 s.

subject: Biology
title: Stroke Volume & EDV
visual_data: SV = EDV - ESV \\ \approx 70\,\text{mL pumped per beat}
description: Blood ejected per ventricular contraction. \(SV\)=stroke volume, \(EDV\)=end-diastolic volume, \(ESV\)=end-systolic volume. Each ventricle pumps ~70 mL per beat.

subject: Biology
title: Nephron Structure
description: Functional unit of kidney. Filtration (Glomerulus) -> Reabsorption (PCT) -> Concentration (Loop of Henle) -> Secretion (DCT) -> Collection.
visual_data: <svg viewBox='0 0 300 150' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><circle cx='30' cy='50' r='20' fill='none' stroke='#F59E0B' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M50,50 Q80,20 100,50' fill='none' stroke='#F59E0B' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M100,50 L100,120 Q120,140 140,120 L140,50' fill='none' stroke='#F59E0B' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M140,50 Q160,20 190,50' fill='none' stroke='#F59E0B' stroke-width='3'/><line x1='190' y1='30' x2='190' y2='140' stroke='#F59E0B' stroke-width='4'/><text x='10' y='20' font-size='10'>Glomerulus</text><text x='60' y='30' font-size='10'>PCT</text><text x='100' y='145' font-size='10'>Henle Loop</text><text x='160' y='30' font-size='10'>DCT</text></svg>

subject: Biology
title: Counter Current Mechanism
visual_data: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path d='M60,20 L60,160 Q80,180 100,160 L100,20' fill='none' stroke='#F59E0B' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M120,20 L120,160 Q140,180 160,160 L160,20' fill='none' stroke='#EF4444' stroke-width='3'/><text x='30' y='90' font-size='10' transform='rotate(90 30,90)'>Henle Loop</text><text x='180' y='90' font-size='10' transform='rotate(90 180,90)'>Vasa Recta</text><text x='80' y='190' font-size='10' text-anchor='middle'>High Osmolarity (1200)</text><text x='80' y='15' font-size='10' text-anchor='middle'>Cortex (300)</text><path d='M70,50 L90,50' stroke='#000' marker-end='url(#arrow)'/><path d='M130,130 L150,130' stroke='#000' marker-end='url(#arrow)'/></svg>
description: Henle's Loop and Vasa Recta. Multiplies osmolarity from 300 (Cortex) to 1200 mOsm (Medulla). Essential for concentrating urine.
derivation: NaCl transported by ascending limb exchanged with descending Vasa Recta.

subject: Biology
title: Haemodialysis
description: Artificial Kidney. Blood pumped into unit with dialysing fluid (same composition as plasma except nitrogenous waste). Waste diffuses out.
visual_data:
Anti-coagulant used: Heparin
Principle: Diffusion across semi-permeable cellophane membrane

subject: Biology
title: RAAS Mechanism
description: Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System. Regulation of GFR. Low BP -> JG Cells release Renin -> Angiotensinogen to Angiotensin II -> Aldosterone (Adrenal Cortex).

subject: Biology
title: GFR (Glomerular Filtration)
description: Amount of filtrate formed by both kidneys per minute. \(GFR\)=Glomerular Filtration Rate; regulated by JGA (Juxtaglomerular Apparatus).

subject: Biology
title: Filtrate Reabsorption
description: Of ~180 L filtrate/day nearly all is reabsorbed, leaving ~1.5 L urine. \(99\%\) of filtrate reabsorbed by tubules.

subject: Biology
title: PCT Reabsorption
description: Proximal Convoluted Tubule is the major site of reabsorption. Nearly all glucose, amino acids and ~70-80% of Na+, water reabsorbed here.

subject: Biology
title: Sarcomere (Muscle)
description: Contractile unit. Z-line to Z-line. A-band (Dark, Myosin+Actin), I-band (Light, Actin only), H-zone (Myosin only).
visual_data: <svg viewBox='0 0 300 100' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='10' y1='10' x2='10' y2='90' stroke='#000' stroke-width='4'/><line x1='290' y1='10' x2='290' y2='90' stroke='#000' stroke-width='4'/><line x1='10' y1='30' x2='100' y2='30' stroke='#3B82F6' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='10' y1='70' x2='100' y2='70' stroke='#3B82F6' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='200' y1='30' x2='290' y2='30' stroke='#3B82F6' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='200' y1='70' x2='290' y2='70' stroke='#3B82F6' stroke-width='2'/><rect x='80' y='40' width='140' height='20' fill='#EF4444'/><text x='150' y='95' text-anchor='middle' font-size='10'>A-Band</text><text x='50' y='95' text-anchor='middle' font-size='10'>I-Band</text><text x='150' y='20' text-anchor='middle' font-size='10'>H-Zone</text></svg>

subject: Biology
title: Sliding Filament Theory
visual_data: \text{Actin slides over Myosin} \to \text{Sarcomere Shortens} \\ \text{H-zone disappears, I-band shortens, A-band constant}
description: Mechanism of muscle contraction. Calcium binds Troponin $\to$ Unmasks Actin $\to$ Myosin head binds $\to$ Power stroke (ATP hydrolysis).
derivation: Cross-bridge cycle: Formation $\to$ Rotation $\to$ Detachment.

subject: Biology
title: Types of Joints
description: Fibrous (Skull sutures - No movement). Cartilaginous (Vertebrae - Slight movement). Synovial (Fluid filled - Free movement).
visual_data:
Ball & Socket: Shoulder/Hip
Hinge: Elbow/Knee
Pivot: Atlas & Axis
Gliding: Carpals
Saddle: Thumb

subject: Biology
title: Human Skeleton (206 Bones)
description: Axial (80): Skull (22), Vertebral Column (26), Sternum (1), Ribs (12 pairs). Appendicular (126): Limbs (30x4), Girdles (Pectoral 4, Pelvic 2).

subject: Biology
title: Muscular Disorders
description: Myasthenia Gravis (Autoimmune - affects NMJ). Muscular Dystrophy (Genetic - degeneration). Tetany (Low Ca++ - spasms). Gout (Uric acid crystals in joints).
visual_data:
Osteoporosis: Age-related, Decreased bone mass (Low Estrogen)
Arthritis: Inflammation of joints

subject: Biology
title: Skeletal Muscle Proteins
visual_data: \text{Thin Filament: Actin + Tropomyosin + Troponin} \\ \text{Thick Filament: Myosin} \\ \text{Troponin } \to \text{ binds } Ca^{2+} \text{ to expose active site}
description: Composition of muscle contractile filaments. Thin filament = F-actin with regulatory proteins tropomyosin and troponin; thick filament = myosin polymer.

subject: Biology
title: Excitation-Contraction Steps
visual_data: \text{ACh} \to \text{Action potential} \to Ca^{2+} \text{ release} \\ Ca^{2+} + \text{Troponin} \to \text{actin sites exposed} \\ \text{Cross-bridge} \to \text{power stroke} \to \text{relax}
description: Sequence of neuromuscular contraction. Neurotransmitter is acetylcholine (ACh); \(Ca^{2+}\) from sarcoplasmic reticulum triggers cross-bridge cycling.

subject: Biology
title: Red vs White Muscle Fibres
description: Comparison of muscle fibre types. Red (Type I) = aerobic, fatigue-resistant; White (Type II) = anaerobic, rapid contraction.

subject: Biology
title: Axial vs Appendicular Skeleton
visual_data: \text{Total} = 206 = 80 \text{ (Axial)} + 126 \text{ (Appendicular)} \\ \text{Axial: Skull 22 + Hyoid 1 + Ears 6 + VC 26 + Sternum 1 + Ribs 24} \\ \text{Appendicular: Limbs + Girdles}
description: Division of human skeleton bone counts. Axial = skull, vertebral column (VC), ribs, sternum; Appendicular = limb bones plus pectoral and pelvic girdles.

subject: Biology
title: Skull Bone Count
description: Breakdown of skull bones. Cranium protects brain (8 bones); face has 14 bones; 6 middle-ear ossicles counted separately.

subject: Biology
title: Vertebral Column Formula
visual_data: \text{VC} = 26 \text{ vertebrae} \\ C_7 \, T_{12} \, L_5 \, S_1 \text{ (fused 5)} \, Co_1 \text{ (fused 3-5)} \\ \text{Atlas = C1, holds skull}
description: Adult vertebral column count. Cervical 7, Thoracic 12, Lumbar 5, Sacrum 1 (5 fused), Coccyx 1 (3-5 fused) = 26 total.

subject: Biology
title: Limb Bone Counts
visual_data: \text{Each upper limb} = 30, \quad \text{Each lower limb} = 30 \\ \text{Forelimb: Humerus, Radius, Ulna, 8 Carpals, 5 Metacarpals, 14 Phalanges} \\ \text{Femur = longest bone}
description: Bones per limb. Each upper and lower limb has 30 bones; total limb bones = 120; femur is the longest bone in the body.

subject: Biology
title: Girdle Bone Counts
visual_data: \text{Pectoral girdle: 2 Clavicle + 2 Scapula} = 4 \\ \text{Pelvic girdle: 2 Coxal (Ilium+Ischium+Pubis)} = 2 \\ \text{Acetabulum} \to \text{femur, Glenoid cavity} \to \text{humerus}
description: Shoulder and hip girdle bones. Pectoral = clavicle + scapula; each coxal bone fuses ilium, ischium and pubis.

subject: Biology
title: Types of Movement
visual_data: \text{Amoeboid: pseudopodia (WBC, macrophages)} \\ \text{Ciliary: cilia (trachea, oviduct)} \\ \text{Muscular: contractile proteins (limbs, jaw)}
description: Three categories of human cell/body movement. Amoeboid uses pseudopodia; ciliary uses cilia; muscular uses actin-myosin.

subject: Biology
title: Muscle Tissue Types
visual_data: \text{Skeletal: striated, voluntary, multinucleate} \\ \text{Cardiac: striated, involuntary, branched, intercalated discs} \\ \text{Smooth: unstriated, involuntary, spindle}
description: Three muscle types by structure and control. Skeletal = voluntary striated; cardiac = involuntary striated with intercalated discs; smooth = involuntary unstriated.

subject: Biology
title: Muscle Hierarchy
description: Levels of organisation in skeletal muscle. A muscle is bundles of fibres; each fibre contains myofibrils made of repeating sarcomeres.

subject: Biology
title: Disorders of Muscular System
visual_data: \text{Myasthenia gravis: autoimmune, } \downarrow \text{ACh receptors} \to \text{fatigue} \\ \text{Muscular dystrophy: genetic, progressive degeneration} \\ \text{Tetany: } \downarrow Ca^{2+} \to \text{rapid spasms}
description: Key NEET muscular disorders. Myasthenia gravis is autoimmune; muscular dystrophy is genetic; tetany results from low blood calcium.

subject: Biology
title: Skeletal Disorders
visual_data: \text{Gout: uric acid crystals in joints} \\ \text{Rheumatoid arthritis: autoimmune joint inflammation} \\ \text{Osteoporosis: } \downarrow \text{estrogen} \to \downarrow \text{bone mass}
description: Joint and bone disorders for NEET. Gout = uric acid deposition; rheumatoid arthritis = autoimmune; osteoporosis = age/hormone-linked bone loss.

subject: Biology
title: Calvin Cycle (C3)
description: 1. Carboxylation (RuBP + CO2 -> 3-PGA). 2. Reduction (ATP+NADPH used). 3. Regeneration of RuBP (ATP used).

subject: Biology
title: C4 Pathway (Hatch & Slack)
description: Kranz Anatomy. Mesophyll: PEPCase fixes CO2 -> OAA (C4). Bundle Sheath: Decarboxylation releases CO2 for RuBisCO (C3 cycle). No Photorespiration.

subject: Biology
title: Z-Scheme (Light Reaction)
description: Non-cyclic photophosphorylation. PS-II (680nm) -> Plastoquinone -> Cytochrome -> PS-I (700nm) -> Ferredoxin -> NADP+.

subject: Biology
title: Blackman's Law of Limiting Factors
description: Photosynthesis rate is limited by the factor in shortest supply (CO2, Light, Temp, Water). Usually CO2 is the limiting factor for C3 plants.
derivation: Light saturation at 10% of full sunlight.

subject: Biology
title: Photorespiration (C2 Cycle)
description: Wasteful process in C3 plants when RuBisCO binds O2 instead of CO2. Occurs in Chloroplast -> Peroxisome -> Mitochondria. No ATP/Sugar produced.

subject: Biology
title: Photosynthetic Pigments
description: Chlorophyll a (Bright green - Primary pigment). Chlorophyll b (Yellow green). Xanthophylls (Yellow). Carotenoids (Yellow-Orange).
visual_data: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 100' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path d='M10,90 Q50,10 90,90' fill='none' stroke='#10B981' stroke-width='2'/><text x='50' y='20' font-size='8' fill='#10B981'>Chl a (Blue/Red absorption)</text><path d='M110,90 Q150,30 190,90' fill='none' stroke='#F59E0B' stroke-width='2'/><text x='150' y='40' font-size='8' fill='#F59E0B'>Carotenoids</text><text x='100' y='95' text-anchor='middle' font-size='8'>Absorption Spectrum</text></svg>

subject: Biology
title: Overall Photosynthesis Equation
description: Net balanced equation of photosynthesis (van Niel's version, showing water on both sides). \(6H_2O\) on RHS is newly formed; \(O_2\) released comes entirely from the 12 water molecules split.

subject: Biology
title: ATP & NADPH per CO2 (Calvin Cycle)
description: Assimilatory power needed to fix CO2 in the C3 (Calvin) cycle. For 1 glucose, 6 turns of cycle are required: \(6\times3=18\) ATP and \(6\times2=12\) NADPH.

subject: Biology
title: C4 Pathway ATP Cost
description: Energy cost of CO2 fixation in C4 plants is higher due to extra ATP for PEP regeneration. \(2\) extra ATP per CO2 to regenerate PEP from pyruvate in mesophyll.

subject: Biology
title: Carbon Count in C3 Cycle
description: First stable product of Calvin cycle is a 3-carbon acid (3-PGA), giving C3 plants their name. RuBP (5C) + CO2 yields an unstable 6C intermediate splitting into two 3C molecules.

subject: Biology
title: C4 First Product (OAA)
description: First stable product in C4 (Hatch-Slack) pathway is oxaloacetic acid, a 4-carbon acid. Primary CO2 acceptor is PEP (3C), enzyme is PEPcase in mesophyll cells.

subject: Biology
title: Emerson's Quantum Yield
description: Emerson enhancement effect: combined illumination at far-red (\(700\,nm\)) and red (\(680\,nm\)) gives photosynthesis greater than sum of both alone, proving two photosystems exist.

subject: Biology
title: Photosystem Reaction Centre Wavelengths
description: Peak absorption wavelengths of the reaction centre chlorophyll-a in each photosystem. PS-I absorbs at \(700\,nm\), PS-II at \(680\,nm\); used to identify the two photosystems.

subject: Biology
title: Visible / PAR Wavelength Range
description: Photosynthetically Active Radiation: the band of visible light driving photosynthesis. Chlorophyll-a absorbs maximally in blue (\(\sim430\,nm\)) and red (\(\sim660\,nm\)) regions.

subject: Biology
title: C4 Leaf Anatomy (Kranz)
visual_data: \text{Bundle sheath cells: large, thick-walled, } O_2\text{-poor, agranal chloroplasts}
description: Kranz anatomy is the defining feature of C4 leaves. Bundle sheath cells encircle vascular bundles in a wreath, have many chloroplasts (often agranal) and no intercellular spaces, concentrating CO2 around RuBisCO.

subject: Biology
title: Nerve Impulse
description: Resting Potential (-70mV, Na+/K+ pump). Depolarization (Na+ influx). Repolarization (K+ efflux).
visual_data: <svg viewBox='0 0 300 100' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='10' y1='80' x2='290' y2='80' stroke='#6B7280'/><line x1='30' y1='10' x2='30' y2='90' stroke='#6B7280'/><path d='M30,70 L80,70 L100,10 L120,90 L150,70 L280,70' fill='none' stroke='#8B5CF6' stroke-width='2'/><text x='40' y='65' font-size='10'>-70mV</text><text x='105' y='25' font-size='10'>+30mV</text><text x='100' y='98' font-size='10' text-anchor='middle'>Action Potential</text></svg>

subject: Biology
title: Synaptic Transmission
description: Electrical signal reaches Axon Terminal -> Ca++ influx -> Vesicles fuse -> Neurotransmitter (Ach) released into Cleft -> Binds to Receptors.

subject: Biology
title: Photoreception Mechanism
description: Light -> Dissociation of Retinal from Opsin -> Opsin structure changes -> Membrane potential changes -> Signal to Ganglion cells.

title: Internal Ear (Cochlea)

title: Human Brain Structure
description: Forebrain (Cerebrum, Thalamus, Hypothalamus). Midbrain (Corpora Quadrigemina). Hindbrain (Pons, Cerebellum, Medulla). Corpus Callosum connects hemispheres.

subject: Biology
title: Reflex Arc
description: Involuntary response. Receptor -> Sensory Neuron (Dorsal root) -> Spinal Cord (Interneuron) -> Motor Neuron (Ventral root) -> Effector (Muscle).

subject: Biology
title: Vestibular Apparatus (Balance)
description: Located above Cochlea. 3 Semicircular canals (Dynamic balance - Crista ampullaris). Otolith organ (Saccule & Utricle - Static balance - Macula).
visual_data:
Crista: Angular acceleration (Rotation)
Macula: Linear acceleration / Gravity (Tilt)

subject: Biology
title: Resting Membrane Potential
description: Polarised potential across axolemma at rest. \(V_{rest}\)=resting potential; membrane more permeable to \(K^+\); maintained by Na\(^+\)/K\(^+\) pump.

related_concepts.name: Polarised membrane
related_concepts.definition: Outer surface positive, inner surface negative due to ionic gradients at rest.

related_concepts.name: Na+/K+ pump
related_concepts.definition: Pumps 3 Na+ out and 2 K+ in per ATP, maintaining concentration gradients.

subject: Biology
title: Action Potential Threshold & Peak
description: Voltage values during nerve impulse. Stimulus must reach threshold \(\approx -55\) mV to fire; reversal of polarity peaks at \(+30\) mV due to Na\(^+\) influx.

subject: Biology
title: Na+/K+ Pump Stoichiometry
description: Active transport ratio maintaining resting potential. For every ATP hydrolysed, 3 Na\(^+\) move out and 2 K\(^+\) move in, creating net negativity inside.

subject: Biology
title: Cranial & Spinal Nerves Count
description: Peripheral Nervous System nerve numbers. \(12\) pairs of cranial nerves arise from brain; \(31\) pairs of spinal nerves arise from spinal cord.

subject: Biology
title: Spinal Nerve Distribution
description: Region-wise split of 31 spinal nerve pairs. \(C\)=cervical(8), \(T\)=thoracic(12), \(L\)=lumbar(5), \(S\)=sacral(5), \(Co\)=coccygeal(1).

subject: Biology
title: Ear Ossicles
description: Three middle-ear bones transmitting vibration. Order from tympanic membrane inward; stapes is the smallest bone in the human body, contacting the oval window.

subject: Biology
title: Rod & Cone Pigments
visual_data: \begin{aligned} \text{Rods} &: \text{Rhodopsin (Vit A + Opsin), dim light} \\ \text{Cones} &: 3\ \text{types (Blue, Green, Red), colour} \end{aligned}
description: Photoreceptor types and pigments. Rods (scotopic) contain rhodopsin for twilight vision; 3 cone types (photopic) enable colour vision and daylight acuity.

subject: Biology
title: Meninges (3 Layers)
description: Three protective membranes of CNS (outer to inner). Dura mater (tough outer), arachnoid (middle), pia mater (delicate inner, adheres to brain).

subject: Biology
title: Repolarisation Ion Movement
description: Ionic basis of action potential phases. Rising phase = Na\(^+\) influx (depolarisation); falling phase = K\(^+\) efflux (repolarisation) restoring negativity.

subject: Biology
title: Brain Major Divisions
description: Three primary regions of the human brain. Forebrain (cerebrum, thalamus, hypothalamus), midbrain (corpora quadrigemina), hindbrain (pons, cerebellum, medulla).

subject: Biology
title: Oxygen Dissociation Curve
description: Sigmoid curve. Right Shift (Bohr Effect): High pCO2, High H+, High Temp (Tissues). Left Shift: Low pCO2, Low Temp (Alveoli).

subject: Biology
title: Glycolysis (EMP Pathway)
description: Occurs in Cytoplasm. Anaerobic. 1 Glucose (6C) -> 2 Pyruvate (3C). Net gain: 2 ATP + 2 NADH.

subject: Biology
title: Krebs Cycle (TCA)
description: Matrix of Mitochondria. Acetyl CoA (2C) + OAA (4C) -> Citrate (6C). Decarboxylation releases 2 CO2. Yields: 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, 1 GTP per cycle.

subject: Biology
title: Respiratory Quotient (RQ)
description: Carbohydrates: 1.0. Fats: 0.7 (Tripalmitin). Proteins: 0.9. Organic Acids: > 1.

subject: Biology
title: Electron Transport System (ETS)
description: Inner Mitochondrial Membrane. Complex I (NADH dehydrogenase), II (Succinate dehydrogenase), III (Cytochrome bc1), IV (Cytochrome c oxidase), V (ATP Synthase). Final acceptor is Oxygen.

subject: Biology
title: ATP Yield Breakdown (Glucose)
description: Stage-wise ATP contribution for one glucose (aerobic). Glycolysis nets 8, link reaction 6, Krebs cycle 24, summing to 38 ATP.

subject: Biology
title: NADH & FADH2 ATP Values
description: Oxidative phosphorylation yield per reducing equivalent via ETS. Each \(NADH\) gives 3 ATP, each \(FADH_2\) gives 2 ATP.

subject: Biology
title: Anaerobic Respiration (Fermentation)
description: Net ATP from fermentation (anaerobic). Only \(2\) ATP per glucose; alcoholic gives ethanol+CO2, lactic acid gives lactate.

subject: Biology
title: RQ of Fat (Tripalmitin)
description: Worked RQ for a typical fat (tripalmitin) showing why fats have \(RQ<1\). 102 CO2 evolved per 145 O2 consumed gives ~0.7.

subject: Biology
title: Glucose Oxidation Balanced Equation
description: Overall balanced equation of aerobic respiration of glucose. 1 glucose + 6 O2 yields 6 CO2 + 6 H2O + energy (RQ = 1).

subject: Biology
title: Krebs Cycle: Per-Turn Yield
description: Products of one turn of TCA cycle per acetyl CoA. Two turns occur per glucose (double all values). GTP equates to 1 ATP.

subject: Biology
title: Pyruvate to Acetyl CoA (Link Reaction)
description: Oxidative decarboxylation connecting glycolysis to Krebs cycle (mitochondrial matrix). Occurs twice per glucose, releasing 2 CO2.

subject: Biology
title: Double Fertilization
description: 1. Syngamy: Male gamete (n) + Egg (n) -> Zygote (2n). 2. Triple Fusion: Male gamete (n) + Polar nuclei (2n) -> PEN (3n).

subject: Biology
title: Embryo Sac Structure
description: Female Gametophyte. 7-celled, 8-nucleate. Egg apparatus (Egg + 2 Synergids) at micropyle. 3 Antipodals at chalaza. Central cell (2 Polar nuclei).

subject: Biology
title: Pollination Agents
description: Anemophily (Wind - Maize, Grasses; non-sticky pollen). Hydrophily (Water - Vallisneria, Zostera). Entomophily (Insect - Yucca/Moth, Amorphophallus).
visual_data:
Wind: Exposed stamens, feathery stigma
Insect: Colorful, Nectar, Sticky pollen
Yucca: Obligate mutualism with Moth

subject: Biology
title: Ploidy of Floral Parts
visual_data: \begin{aligned}\text{Nucellus, MMC} &\to 2n \\ \text{Megaspore, Egg, Synergid} &\to n \\ \text{Antipodals, Polar nuclei} &\to n \\ \text{Secondary nucleus} &\to 2n \\ \text{Endosperm} &\to 3n \\ \text{Perisperm} &\to 2n\end{aligned}
description: Quick ploidy lookup for embryo-sac and ovule structures. \(n\)=haploid, \(2n\)=diploid, \(3n\)=triploid. MMC = Megaspore Mother Cell; perisperm = persistent diploid nucellus.

subject: Biology
title: Embryo Sac Cell/Nucleus Count
description: Standard mature female gametophyte composition (Polygonum type). 8 nuclei but only 7 cells because the central cell holds the 2 polar nuclei.

subject: Biology
title: Megasporogenesis Ratio
description: Megaspore formation in monosporic (Polygonum) development. One diploid megaspore mother cell yields a linear tetrad; only the chalazal megaspore survives.

subject: Biology
title: Microsporogenesis Ratio
description: Pollen formation. One pollen mother cell (microspore mother cell) gives 4 haploid pollen grains; PMC = Pollen Mother Cell.

subject: Biology
title: Pollen Grain Cell Composition
description: Male gametophyte structure. ~60% of angiosperms shed pollen at 2-celled stage; ~40% at 3-celled stage. Generative cell divides to form 2 male gametes.

subject: Biology
title: Anther Wall Layers
description: Sequence of microsporangium wall layers. Tapetum (innermost) nourishes developing pollen; endothecium aids dehiscence.

subject: Biology
title: Pollen Viability Range
description: Duration pollen stays viable after release; varies by family. Pollen cryopreserved in liquid nitrogen for crop breeding (pollen banks).

subject: Biology
title: Triple Fusion vs Syngamy
visual_data: \text{Syngamy: male gamete (n)} + \text{egg (n)} \to \text{zygote (2n)} \\ \text{Triple fusion: male gamete (n)} + 2\ \text{polar nuclei (n+n)} \to \text{PEN (3n)}
description: The two fusion events of double fertilization. PEN = Primary Endosperm Nucleus (3n); one male gamete fuses with egg, the other with the central cell.

subject: Biology
title: Polyembryony (Citrus)
description: More than one embryo per seed, classic in Citrus and Mango. Extra embryos arise from diploid nucellus, so they are clonal (apomictic).

subject: Biology
title: Seed = Fertilized Ovule
description: Post-fertilization fate of floral structures. Standard one-to-one transformation table tested frequently in NEET assertion-reason questions.

subject: Biology
title: Dicot vs Monocot Embryo Cotyledons
description: Cotyledon number distinguishing the two embryo types. Monocot embryo has coleoptile (shoot) and coleorhiza (root) sheaths.

subject: Biology
title: Endosperm Type by Persistence
visual_data: \text{Albuminous (endospermic):}\ \text{endosperm persists} \\ (\text{maize, castor, wheat, coconut, barley}) \\ \text{Non-albuminous (ex-albuminous):}\ \text{endosperm consumed} \\ (\text{pea, groundnut, bean})
description: Classification of seeds by whether triploid endosperm remains at maturity. Frequently tested example-matching fact.

subject: Biology
title: Coconut Endosperm States
description: Classic NEET example of nuclear endosperm. Coconut water is the syncytial free-nuclear stage; the surrounding white kernel is the later cellular endosperm.

subject: Biology
title: Parthenocarpic vs True Fruit
visual_data: \text{True fruit: from ovary only} \\ \text{False fruit: thalamus contributes (apple, cashew)} \\ \text{Parthenocarpic: seedless, no fertilization (banana)}
description: Fruit classification by origin. Parthenocarpy gives seedless fruit (induced by growth hormones); false fruit involves accessory floral parts.

subject: Biology
title: Lac Operon
description: Inducible operon. In absence of lactose, Repressor binds Operator. In presence, Inducer (Lactose) binds Repressor, allowing Transcription.

subject: Biology
title: Linkage (Morgan)
description: Physical association of genes on same chromosome. Inversely proportional to distance.

subject: Biology
title: Chromosomal Disorders
description: Aneuploidy (Non-disjunction). Down's (Trisomy 21). Klinefelter's (XXY - Sterile male). Turner's (XO - Sterile female).
visual_data:
Down's Syndrome: 47, XX, +21
Klinefelter's: 47, XXY (Gynecomastia)
Turner's: 45, XO (Rudimentary Ovaries)

subject: Biology
title: Co-dominance (Blood Groups)
description: Both alleles express themselves fully in heterozygotes. Example: ABO Blood Grouping (IA and IB are co-dominant).
visual_data: I^A I^B \to \text{Group AB} \\ I^A i \to \text{Group A} \\ ii \to \text{Group O}

subject: Biology
title: Genetic Mapping
description: Alfred Sturtevant. Distance between genes is proportional to recombination frequency. 1% Recombination = 1 map unit (cM).

subject: Biology
title: Types of Mutation
visual_data: \text{Point: Change in single base pair (Sickle Cell)} \\ \text{Frameshift: Insertion/Deletion (Thalassemia)}
description: Sickle Cell: GAG $\to$ GUG (Glu $\to$ Val). Frame shift changes the entire reading frame.
derivation: Mutagens: UV rays, chemical agents.

subject: Biology
title: Sex Determination
visual_data: \text{XX-XY: Human, Drosophila (Male Het)} \\ \text{XX-XO: Grasshopper (Male Het)} \\ \text{ZZ-ZW: Birds (Female Het)}
description: Heterogametic sex produces two types of gametes determining the sex of offspring.
derivation: Haplodiploidy in Honeybees.

subject: Biology
title: Test Cross
description: Cross between dominant phenotype (unknown genotype) and recessive parent. Used to determine if individual is Homozygous (TT) or Heterozygous (Tt).
visual_data: \text{If 100\% Tall} \to \text{Parent was TT} \\ \text{If 50\% Tall, 50\% Dwarf} \to \text{Parent was Tt}

subject: Biology
title: Polygenic Inheritance
description: Quantitative inheritance. Trait controlled by 3 or more genes. Additive effect. Example: Human Skin Color (AABBCC = Darkest, aabbcc = Lightest).

subject: Biology
title: Mendelian Disorders
description: Haemophilia (Sex-linked Recessive - Clotting defect). Sickle Cell Anemia (Autosomal Recessive - HbS). Phenylketonuria (Inborn error of metabolism).
visual_data: \text{Haemophilia: X-linked (Carrier female transmits to son)} \\ \text{Sickle Cell: Glu } \to \text{ Val at 6th pos of } \beta \text{-chain}

subject: Biology
title: Color Blindness
description: Sex-linked recessive disorder. Defect in Red/Green cones. More common in males (8%) than females (0.4%) because males have only one X chromosome.
visual_data: X^C Y \to \text{Affected Male} \\ X^C X \to \text{Carrier Female (Normal Vision)}

subject: Biology
title: Thalassemia
description: Autosomal recessive. Quantitative problem (Reduced synthesis of Globin chains). Alpha Thalassemia (Chr 16). Beta Thalassemia (Chr 11).
visual_data:
Alpha: Genes HBA1, HBA2
Beta: Gene HBB
Result: Anemia

subject: Biology
title: Pedigree: Autosomal vs Sex-Linked
description: Autosomal Dominant: Does not skip generations (Myotonic Dystrophy). Autosomal Recessive: Skips generations (Sickle Cell). Sex-Linked: Criss-cross inheritance (Haemophilia).

subject: Biology
title: Monohybrid Ratio
description: F2 ratio of a single-gene cross (Mendel's pea, Tall x Dwarf). \(TT\)=homozygous dominant, \(Tt\)=heterozygous, \(tt\)=homozygous recessive.

subject: Biology
title: Law of Independent Assortment
description: Mendel's 3rd law: alleles of different genes segregate independently into gametes. Four gamete types in equal 1:1:1:1 proportion.

subject: Biology
title: Number of Gametes / Genotypes
description: Combinations from \(n\) heterozygous gene pairs (complete dominance). \(n\)=number of heterozygous loci. e.g. trihybrid \(n=3 \Rightarrow 8\) gametes, \(27\) genotypes.

subject: Biology
title: Incomplete Dominance
description: F2 of Snapdragon (Antirrhinum) / Mirabilis — phenotype ratio equals genotype ratio, heterozygote is intermediate. \(RR\)=red, \(Rr\)=pink, \(rr\)=white.

subject: Biology
title: Recessive Epistasis (9:3:4)
description: Modified dihybrid ratio where homozygous recessive at one locus (cc) masks the other gene (mouse coat colour). \(9:3:4\) sums the masked classes into one.

subject: Biology
title: Dominant Epistasis (12:3:1)
description: Modified dihybrid ratio where a dominant allele at one locus masks expression of the other gene. Classic gene-interaction variant of 9:3:3:1.

subject: Biology
title: Complementary Genes (9:7)
description: Two genes needed together for a phenotype; either alone gives the recessive phenotype (Bateson & Punnett, Lathyrus). Sums 3:3:1 into the 7.

subject: Biology
title: Human Chromosome Number
description: Diploid set: 22 pairs autosomes + 1 pair sex chromosomes. \(n=23\) in gametes (haploid). Female homogametic (XX), male heterogametic (XY).

subject: Biology
title: ABO Multiple Alleles
visual_data: 3 \text{ alleles: } I^A, I^B, i \\ \to 6 \text{ genotypes}, \; 4 \text{ phenotypes}
description: ABO blood group is governed by multiple alleles; \(I^A,I^B\) dominant over \(i\) and codominant to each other. Phenotypes: A, B, AB, O.

subject: Biology
title: Back Cross vs Test Cross
visual_data: \text{Back cross: } F_1 \times \text{either parent} \\ \text{Test cross: } F_1 \times tt \;(\text{recessive parent})
description: Test cross is the special back cross with the homozygous recessive parent, used to determine an unknown genotype. F1 (Tt) x tt gives 1:1 ratio.

title: PCR Cycles

subject: Biology
title: Restriction Site (EcoRI)
description: Palindromic sequence cut by EcoRI enzyme. Produces sticky ends.

subject: Biology
title: Gel Electrophoresis
description: Separation of DNA fragments by size. DNA is negative (moves to Anode +). Smaller fragments move faster/further.

title: Stirred Tank Bioreactor
description: Used for large scale culture. Agitator mixes oxygen. Sparger introduces air bubbles. Control systems for pH, Temperature, and Foam.

subject: Biology
title: Tissue Culture
description: Totipotency: Capacity of a cell to generate whole plant. Explant grown in nutrient medium. Micropropagation (Somaclones). Virus-free plants (Meristem culture).

subject: Biology
title: Cloning Vectors
description: Vehicles to transfer DNA. Plasmids (Bacteria). Bacteriophage (High copy number). BAC/YAC (For large DNA - HGP). Agrobacterium (Ti plasmid - Plants). Retrovirus (Animals).
visual_data:
Agrobacterium tumifaciens:
Natural Genetic Engineer of plants

subject: Biology
title: DNA Charge & Movement
description: Why DNA moves toward the positive electrode in gel electrophoresis. DNA is negatively charged due to phosphate groups, so fragments migrate from cathode (\(-\)) to anode (\(+\)); smaller fragments travel farther.

subject: Biology
title: Palindrome Sequence
description: Recognition site of restriction enzymes = palindromic sequence (reads same 5'→3' on both strands). Enzymes cut between same two bases on both strands, often leaving single-stranded overhangs called sticky ends.

subject: Biology
title: Salt/Gradient for DNA Isolation
description: DNA is precipitated by adding chilled ethanol and appears as collection of fine threads in suspension. Membranes lysed by lysozyme (bacteria)/cellulase (plant)/chitinase (fungus); RNA removed by RNase, proteins by protease.

subject: Biology
title: Lysing Enzymes (Cell Wall)
description: Enzymes used to break open cells to release DNA, matched to cell-wall composition. Lysozyme for bacterial peptidoglycan, cellulase for plant cellulose, chitinase for fungal chitin.

subject: Biology
title: Ti Plasmid Transfer (T-DNA)
description: Agrobacterium tumefaciens delivers a Tumour-inducing (Ti) plasmid; its T-DNA integrates into the plant cell genome. The disarmed Ti plasmid is used as a cloning vector to transform plant cells.

subject: Biology
title: Selectable Markers (pBR322)
description: Antibiotic-resistance genes act as selectable markers to identify transformants. \(amp^R\) and \(tet^R\) genes in pBR322 let transformed cells survive on antibiotic media while non-transformed cells die.

subject: Biology
title: Insertional Inactivation
description: Screening method: foreign DNA inserted into \(tet^R\) gene of pBR322 disrupts it, so recombinants become tetracycline-sensitive but ampicillin-resistant. Non-recombinants grow on both antibiotics.

subject: Biology
title: Blue-White Selection
description: Modern screening using insertion into \(lacZ\) (β-galactosidase) gene. Insert inactivates the enzyme so no blue colour on chromogenic substrate; recombinant colonies are white, non-recombinants are blue.

subject: Biology
title: PCR Amplification Factor
description: Number of DNA copies after PCR cycles (theoretical doubling each cycle). \(N\)=copies produced, \(n\)=number of cycles; e.g. ~1 billion copies after about 30 cycles.

subject: Biology
title: PCR Enzyme (Taq)
description: Thermostable DNA polymerase used in PCR to extend primers. Taq remains active at the high denaturation temperature (~94°C), avoiding addition of fresh enzyme each cycle.

subject: Biology
title: Gene Gun / Biolistics
description: Direct gene transfer method: high-velocity gold or tungsten microparticles coated with DNA bombard cells. One of the methods to introduce alien DNA into host cells (others: microinjection, disarmed pathogen vectors).

subject: Biology
title: Competent Cell (CaCl2 / Heat Shock)
description: Making bacterial cells competent to take up DNA. Cells treated with divalent cations (\(Ca^{2+}\)) then given a brief heat shock at 42°C (and back on ice) to force recombinant DNA across the membrane.

subject: Biology
title: Origin of Replication (ori)
description: Sequence in a vector where replication starts; controls plasmid copy number. To recover many copies of the target DNA, the vector must have an \(ori\); a high-copy ori gives large numbers of recombinant DNA.

subject: Biology
title: DNA Ligase (Molecular Glue)
description: Enzyme that joins DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds. Compatible sticky ends of vector and foreign DNA (cut by same RE) are sealed by DNA ligase to make recombinant DNA.

subject: Biology
title: Downstream Processing
description: Final stage after bioreactor fermentation before a product is marketed. Product is separated and purified, then formulated with preservatives; clinical products undergo quality control and clinical trials.

subject: Biology
title: Five Kingdom System
description: R.H. Whittaker (1969). Monera (Prokaryote), Protista (Unicellular Eukaryote), Fungi (Chitin wall), Plantae (Cellulose), Animalia (No wall).

subject: Biology
title: Viruses & Viroids
visual_data: \text{Virus: Nucleoprotein (DNA/RNA + Capsid)} \\ \text{Viroid: Free RNA (No coat, Low MW)} \\ \text{Prion: Abnormal Protein}
description: Virus (Ivanowsky/Stanley). Viroid (T.O. Diener - Potato Spindle Tuber). Prion (Mad Cow Disease).
derivation: Connect link between living and non-living.

subject: Biology
title: Bacteriophage Structure
description: Virus that infects bacteria. Polyhedral Head (Capsid containing DNA), Collar, Sheath, Tail Fibres (attachment).

subject: Biology
title: Kingdom Fungi Groups
description: Phycomycetes (Algal - Rhizopus). Ascomycetes (Sac - Yeast, Penicillium). Basidiomycetes (Club - Mushroom/Agaricus, Puccinia). Deuteromycetes (Imperfect - Trichoderma).
visual_data:
Sexual spores:
Ascospores (Endogenous)
Basidiospores (Exogenous)
Deuteromycetes: No sexual stage known

subject: Biology
title: Protozoan Groups
description: Amoeboid (Pseudopodia - Entamoeba). Flagellated (Trypanosoma - Sleeping sickness). Ciliated (Paramoecium - Gullet). Sporozoans (Plasmodium - Malaria).
visual_data:
Heterotrophs (Predators or Parasites)
Primitive relatives of animals

subject: Biology
title: Bacterial Shapes
description: The four basic morphological forms of bacteria. \(\text{Coccus}\)=spherical, \(\text{Bacillus}\)=rod-shaped, \(\text{Vibrio}\)=comma-shaped, \(\text{Spirillum}\)=spiral/helical.

subject: Biology
title: Gram Staining Result
description: Differential staining of bacteria by Christian Gram based on cell wall (peptidoglycan). \(\text{Gram +ve}\)=thick peptidoglycan retains crystal violet (purple); \(\text{Gram -ve}\)=thin wall, takes safranin counterstain (pink).

subject: Biology
title: Five Kingdom Author & Year
description: Proposer and year of the Five Kingdom classification. Criteria used: cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships.

subject: Biology
title: Two Kingdom System
description: The earliest classification dividing all organisms into two kingdoms, given by Linnaeus. It failed to separate prokaryotes/eukaryotes and autotrophs/heterotrophs.

subject: Biology
title: Slime Mould Spore Walls
description: Slime moulds (Protista) under unfavourable conditions form a plasmodium that differentiates into fruiting bodies bearing spores. Spores possess true walls and are extremely resistant, surviving for many years.

subject: Biology
title: Dinoflagellate Flagella
description: Dinoflagellates have two flagella (one longitudinal, one transverse in furrows) causing spinning movement. Rapid multiplication of red dinoflagellates (e.g. Gonyaulax) causes red tides, releasing toxins that kill marine life.

subject: Biology
title: Lichen Symbiosis
description: Symbiotic association in lichens. Algae (autotroph, phycobiont) prepare food; fungi (heterotroph, mycobiont) provide shelter, absorb water and minerals. Lichens are good pollution indicators.

subject: Biology
title: Mycorrhiza Association
description: Symbiotic association between fungal hyphae and roots of higher plants. Fungus absorbs minerals/water for the plant; plant provides sugars to the fungus (e.g. Glomus).

subject: Biology
title: TMV Discovery
description: Tobacco Mosaic Virus milestones. Ivanowsky (1892) showed pathogens smaller than bacteria; Beijerinck called the fluid Contagium vivum fluidum; W.M. Stanley (1935) crystallized viruses (proteinaceous).

subject: Biology
title: Mycoplasma Features
description: Mycoplasma are organisms that completely lack a cell wall, are the smallest known living cells, can survive without oxygen (anaerobic) and are pathogenic in animals and plants.

subject: Biology
title: Diatom Cell Wall
description: Chrysophytes/diatoms have indestructible silica (SiO2) cell walls forming two thin overlapping shells (like a soap box). Their cell wall deposits over ages form diatomaceous earth, used in polishing and filtration.

subject: Biology
title: Euglenoid Nutrition
description: Euglenoids (e.g. Euglena) are mixotrophic: photosynthetic (autotrophic) in presence of sunlight but behave as heterotrophs (predators on smaller organisms) when deprived of light. They have a protein-rich flexible pellicle instead of a cell wall.

subject: Biology
title: Archaebacteria Types
description: Archaebacteria live in extreme habitats. Halophiles (extreme salt), Thermoacidophiles (hot acidic springs), Methanogens (marshy/gut of ruminants, produce methane/biogas). Their cell wall has a different (branched-chain lipid) structure enabling survival.

subject: Biology
title: Root Modifications
description: Storage (Carrot - Conical, Radish - Fusiform). Support (Banyan - Prop, Maize - Stilt). Respiration (Rhizophora - Pneumatophores).

subject: Biology
title: Aestivation Types
description: Arrangement of sepals/petals. Valvate (Calotropis), Twisted (Cotton), Imbricate (Cassia), Vexillary (Pea/Bean).

subject: Biology
title: Placentation Types
description: Arrangement of ovules. Marginal (Pea), Axile (Lemon, Tomato), Parietal (Mustard), Free Central (Dianthus), Basal (Sunflower).
visual_data:
Marginal: Ridge (Pea)
Axile: Central Axis (Tomato)
Parietal: Inner Wall (Mustard)
Basal: Base (Sunflower)

subject: Biology
title: Inflorescence Types
description: Racemose: Main axis continues growth, flowers acropetal (bottom-old, top-young). Cymose: Main axis terminates in flower, basipetal order.

subject: Biology
title: Floral Symmetry
description: Actinomorphic (Radial) - cut in any plane (Mustard, Datura). Zygomorphic (Bilateral) - cut in one plane (Pea, Bean, Gulmohar).

subject: Biology
title: Floral Formula Symbols
derivation: Standard technical description of flowering plants.

subject: Biology
title: Fruit Types
description: True Fruit: Developed from ovary. False Fruit: Thalamus contributes (Apple, Strawberry). Parthenocarpic: Without fertilization.
derivation: Mango: Edible part is Mesocarp.

subject: Biology
title: Leaf Phyllotaxy
description: Pattern of leaf arrangement. Alternate (China Rose - 1 per node). Opposite (Guava - 2 per node). Whorled (Alstonia - >2 per node).

subject: Biology
title: Dicot vs Monocot Seed
description: Dicot: 2 Cotyledons, Embryonal axis (Plumule/Radicle). Monocot: 1 Cotyledon (Scutellum), Aleurone layer (Protein), Endosperm (Food).

subject: Biology
title: Stem Modifications
description: Storage (Potato/Tuber, Ginger/Rhizome, Colocasia/Corm). Support (Tendrils - Cucumber). Protection (Thorns - Citrus). Photosynthesis (Phylloclade - Opuntia).
visual_data:
Offset: Aquatic (Pistia, Eichhornia)
Sucker: Chrysanthemum, Banana
Runner: Grasses

subject: Biology
title: Family Solanaceae (Potato)
description: Vegetables (Potato, Tomato, Brinjal), Spice (Chilli), Medicine (Belladonna, Ashwagandha), Fumigatory (Tobacco).

subject: Biology
title: Family Fabaceae (Pea/Bean)
description: Pulses (Gram, Arhar), Edible oil (Soybean, Groundnut), Dye (Indigofera), Fibres (Sunhemp), Fodder (Sesbania).

subject: Biology
title: Family Liliaceae (Lily)
description: Ornamentals (Tulip, Gloriosa), Medicine (Aloe), Vegetables (Asparagus), Colchicine (Colchicum autumnale).

subject: Biology
title: Family Brassicaceae Formula
description: Floral formula of Cruciferae/Brassicaceae (Mustard). \(K\)=calyx (4 sepals in 2 whorls), \(C\)=corolla (4 petals, cruciform), \(A\)=androecium (6 stamens, tetradynamous 2+4), \(\underline{G}_{(2)}\)=bicarpellary syncarpous superior ovary.

subject: Biology
title: Tetradynamous Stamens
description: Stamen condition in Brassicaceae/Mustard. \(A_{2+4}\)=six stamens of which four are long (inner whorl) and two are short (outer whorl).

subject: Biology
title: Stamen Cohesion Numbers
description: Number of stamen bundles by filament fusion. Monadelphous=all united into one group; Diadelphous=two groups (9)+1; Polyadelphous=more than two groups.

subject: Biology
title: Marginal vs Other Carpel No.
description: Carpel number notation in gynoecium. \(G_1\)=monocarpellary (one carpel, e.g. Pea); \(G_2\)=bicarpellary; bracket \(()\)=syncarpous (fused), no bracket=apocarpous (free).

subject: Biology
title: Trimerous vs Pentamerous
description: Floral merosity distinguishing the two classes. Trimerous=floral whorls in multiples of 3 (monocots); tetra-/pentamerous=multiples of 4 or 5 (dicots).

subject: Biology
title: Venation: Reticulate vs Parallel
description: Leaf venation pattern as a class indicator. Reticulate=network of veins (dicots); Parallel=veins run parallel (monocots).

subject: Biology
title: Root System by Class
description: Primary root fate distinguishing classes. Tap root=persistent primary root with branches (dicots); Fibrous=primary root replaced by adventitious roots (monocots).

subject: Biology
title: Epigynous Ovary Position
description: Ovary position relative to other whorls. \(\underline{G}\)=superior ovary, hypogynous flower (mustard, brinjal); \(\overline{G}\)=inferior ovary, epigynous flower (guava, cucumber, sunflower ray florets).

subject: Biology
title: Cohesion of Petals/Sepals
description: Bracket notation for fusion within a whorl. Subscript in bracket \((5)\)=fused (gamosepalous/gamopetalous); plain \(5\)=free (polysepalous/polypetalous).

subject: Biology
title: Number of Floral Whorls
visual_data: \text{Complete flower} = K + C + A + G \ (4 \text{ whorls})
description: A complete flower bears all four whorls. \(K\)=calyx, \(C\)=corolla, \(A\)=androecium, \(G\)=gynoecium; if any whorl is absent the flower is incomplete.

subject: Biology
title: Perianth Notation
description: Used when sepals and petals are indistinguishable. \(P\)=perianth made of tepals; in Liliaceae \(P_{(3+3)}\)=two trimerous whorls fused.

subject: Biology
title: ART Techniques
description: Assisted Reproductive Technologies. IVF (In Vitro), ET (Embryo Transfer).

subject: Biology
title: Infertility Treatments
description: ZIFT (Zygote -> Fallopian). IUT (Embryo > 8 cells -> Uterus). GIFT (Gamete -> Fallopian). ICSI (Sperm injected into Ovum).
visual_data:
ZIFT: Zygote to Fallopian
IUT: Embryo (>8 blastomeres) to Uterus
GIFT: Gamete transfer (requires functional tube)
ICSI: Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection

subject: Biology
title: Contraceptive Methods
description: Barrier (Condoms, Diaphragms). IUDs (Copper T - suppress motility; LNG-20 - hormone releasing). Oral Pills (Saheli - Non-steroidal, Centchroman).
visual_data:
Surgical: Vasectomy (Male), Tubectomy (Female)
Natural: Periodic Abstinence, Withdrawal, Lactational Amenorrhea

subject: Biology
title: MTP (Medical Termination of Pregnancy)
description: Legalized in India 1971. Safe up to 1st Trimester (12 weeks). Used for contraceptive failure, rape, or health risk.

subject: Biology
title: RCH Programme Year
description: Landmark year/scheme for reproductive health in India. India was among the first countries to initiate 'Family Planning' in 1951; later programmes are called RCH programmes.

subject: Biology
title: Population Growth Rate
description: Alarming population growth figure quoted in NCERT. Annual growth rate ~1.7% implies population doubling in about 33 years; total fertility rate (TFR) target reduced over decades.

subject: Biology
title: India Population Figures
description: Census figures NCERT uses to show population explosion. Population rose from 238 million (1900) to over 1 billion (2000) to 1.2 billion (May 2011).

subject: Biology
title: Legal Marriage Age
description: Statutory marriageable age advocated to control population. Raising marriage age of females to 18 yr and males to 21 yr is a key measure.

subject: Biology
title: Ideal Family Norm
description: Recommended small-family norm and motivational slogan to limit family size. Couples encouraged to have not more than two children.

subject: Biology
title: MTP Safe Limit
description: Gestational cut-off for relatively safe medical termination of pregnancy. Abortions during the first trimester (up to 12 weeks) are far safer than second-trimester ones.

subject: Biology
title: MTP Legalisation Year
description: Year the Government of India legalised medical termination of pregnancy with strict conditions to curb illegal abortions and female foeticide.

subject: Biology
title: IUD Examples
description: Standard classification of intra-uterine devices by type. Cu ions suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity; hormonal IUDs make uterus unsuitable for implantation and cervix hostile to sperms.

subject: Biology
title: Emergency Contraception Window
description: Time limit for emergency (post-coital) contraception to avoid pregnancy. Progestogens / progestogen-estrogen combinations or IUDs work if administered within 72 hr of intercourse or sexual assault.

subject: Biology
title: Lactational Amenorrhea
description: Natural contraception based on absence of ovulation/menstruation during intense breast-feeding. Chances of conception near zero up to about 6 months after parturition; no side effects.

subject: Biology
title: IVF / Test-Tube Baby Transfer
description: Blastomere-number criterion deciding the site of embryo transfer in IVF. In-vitro fertilisation forms a zygote; an early embryo (up to 8 blastomeres) goes into the fallopian tube while a later embryo (>8 blastomeres) goes into the uterus.

subject: Biology
title: Condom Brand
description: Standard NCERT example of a popular barrier contraceptive for males. Condoms (e.g., Nirodh) made of thin rubber/latex sheath; also reduce STI/HIV transmission.

subject: Biology
title: Female Barrier Devices
description: Reusable female barrier contraceptives that cover the cervix. Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are made of rubber and inserted to block sperm entry through the cervix; used with spermicides.

subject: Biology
title: Homologous Organs
description: Same origin, different function. Evidence of Divergent Evolution.

subject: Biology
title: Hardy-Weinberg Factors
description: 5 Factors affecting equilibrium: Gene Migration, Genetic Drift (Founder/Bottleneck), Mutation, Recombination, Natural Selection.
visual_data:
Equilibrium: p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1

Disrupted by:
1. Gene Flow
2. Genetic Drift
3. Mutation
4. Recombination
5. Natural Selection

subject: Biology
title: Analogous Organs
description: Different origin, Same function. Evidence of Convergent Evolution. Wings of Butterfly vs Bat. Eye of Octopus vs Mammal.
visual_data: \text{Wings: Insect vs Bird} \\ \text{Eye: Octopus vs Mammal} \\ \text{Sweet Potato (Root) vs Potato (Stem)}

subject: Biology
title: Hardy-Weinberg Equation
description: Allele frequencies remain constant in absence of disturbing factors. Sum of frequencies is 1.
visual_data: \begin{aligned} p + q = 1 \\ p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1 \\ (p^2 \text{ AA}, q^2 \text{ aa}, 2pq \text{ Aa}) \end{aligned}

subject: Biology
title: Miller-Urey Experiment
description: Chemical Evolution. Simulated primitive earth: CH4, NH3, H2, Water vapor at 800°C + Electric Discharge. Result: Amino Acids formed.

subject: Biology
title: Adaptive Radiation
description: Evolution of different species from a common ancestor starting in a geographical area and radiating to other habitats. Ex: Darwin's Finches, Australian Marsupials.
visual_data:
Darwin's Finches: Beak shape changed based on food (Seed, Insect, Cactus)
Marsupials: Wolf, Tiger Cat, Anteater (all marsupial)

subject: Biology
title: Human Evolution
description: Dryopithecus (Ape-like) -> Ramapithecus -> Australopithecus (2mya, Fruit) -> Homo habilis (First human-like, 650cc) -> Homo erectus (Meat eater, 900cc) -> Homo sapiens.

subject: Biology
title: Industrial Melanism
description: Natural Selection evidence. England (1850s): White moths > Dark moths (Lichens on trees). England (1920s): Dark moths > White moths (Smoke/Soot killed lichens).

subject: Biology
title: Theories of Origin of Life
description: Panspermia (Spores from space). Spontaneous Generation (Disproved by Louis Pasteur). Chemical Evolution (Oparin & Haldane - Life from non-living organic molecules).
visual_data:
Pasteur's Swan Neck Flask Experiment:
Life comes only from pre-existing life (Biogenesis)

subject: Biology
title: Divergent vs Convergent
description: Homologous (Divergent): Same origin (Vertebrate heart/brain). Analogous (Convergent): Different origin (Potato/Sweet Potato, Flippers of Penguin/Dolphin).

subject: Biology
title: Geological Time Scale
description: Paleozoic (Invertebrates/Fish). Mesozoic (Reptiles/Dinosaurs). Cenozoic (Mammals/Humans).
visual_data:
Jurassic: Age of Dinosaurs
Devonian: Age of Fishes
Carboniferous: Coal formation

subject: Biology
title: Oparin-Haldane Hypothesis
visual_data: \text{Inorganic} \xrightarrow{\text{energy}} \text{Organic (abiogenic)} \\ \text{Atmosphere: } CH_4, NH_3, H_2, \text{ water vapour} \\ \text{Reducing, } O_2 \text{ absent}
description: Chemical evolution: first life arose from non-living organic molecules under a reducing primitive atmosphere. Lists the assumed primitive gases.

subject: Biology
title: Cosmozoic / Panspermia
visual_data: \text{Life (spores/units)} \rightarrow \text{from outer space} \\ \text{aka Theory of Cosmozoic / Panspermia}
description: Theory that life-forms (spores) reached Earth from outer space. A standard 'theories of origin of life' recall point distinct from biogenesis/abiogenesis.

subject: Biology
title: Sickle-Cell & Malaria (Heterozygote Advantage)
visual_data: Hb^A Hb^S \rightarrow \text{malaria resistant} \\ Hb^S Hb^S \rightarrow \text{sickle cell anaemia (lethal)} \\ \text{Selection maintains } Hb^S \text{ in malarial zones}
description: Classic example of natural selection / balanced polymorphism: heterozygote is fitter in malaria-endemic regions, keeping the sickle allele frequent.

subject: Biology
title: Darwin Voyage & Galapagos
visual_data: \text{Ship: HMS Beagle} \\ \text{Finch species observed} = 13 \\ \text{Book (1859): On the Origin of Species}
description: Fixed factual values around Darwinian evolution: the 13 finch species of the Galapagos and the 1859 publication — direct one-mark recall.

subject: Biology
title: Antibody Structure (IgG)
description: Y-shaped protein. H2L2 (2 Heavy chains, 2 Light chains). Disulfide bonds connect chains. Antigen binding site at tips (Variable region).
