subject: Biology
title: HIV Replication
description: Retrovirus. RNA genome -> Reverse Transcription (Viral DNA) -> Integration into Host Genome -> Transcription -> New Viral RNA.

subject: Biology
title: Drug Sources
description: Opioids (Poppy - Papaver somniferum), Cannabinoids (Cannabis sativa), Coca alkaloid (Erythroxylum coca).

subject: Biology
title: Active vs Passive Immunity
description: Active: Body makes antibodies (Vaccine/Infection, Slow, Long-lasting). Passive: Ready-made antibodies (Colostrum IgA, Anti-venom, Fast, Short-lived).
visual_data:
Active: Vaccine, Infection (Memory present)
Passive: Colostrum, Tetanus shot (No Memory)

subject: Biology
title: Vaccination Types
description: Live Attenuated (MMR, OPV). Killed/Inactivated (Rabies, IPV). Toxoid (Tetanus, Diphtheria). Subunit (Hepatitis B - Yeast derived).
visual_data:
Live: Polio (Oral), BCG
Killed: Polio (Injectable), Cholera
Toxoid: Tetanus
Recombinant: Hep-B

subject: Biology
title: Malaria Lifecycle
description: Infective stage: Sporozoites (Mosquito bite). Liver: Asexual reproduction. RBCs: Rupture releases Haemozoin (Fever/Chills). Gametocytes formed in Human, fertilization in Mosquito gut.
visual_data: <svg viewBox='0 0 300 150' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='60' width='130' height='80' fill='#FECACA' rx='10'/> <text x='75' y='130' text-anchor='middle' font-size='10' fill='#EF4444'>Human Host</text> <rect x='160' y='60' width='130' height='80' fill='#BFDBFE' rx='10'/> <text x='225' y='130' text-anchor='middle' font-size='10' fill='#3B82F6'>Mosquito Host</text> <circle cx='40' cy='90' r='15' fill='#7F1D1D'/> <text x='40' y='110' font-size='8' fill='#fff' text-anchor='middle'>Liver</text> <circle cx='100' cy='90' r='10' fill='#EF4444'/> <text x='100' y='110' font-size='8' fill='#fff' text-anchor='middle'>RBC</text> <path d='M100,80 L160,20 L220,80 L160,140 L100,80' fill='none' stroke='#000' stroke-dasharray='4,2'/> <text x='160' y='20' text-anchor='middle' font-size='10'>Sporozoites</text> <text x='160' y='145' text-anchor='middle' font-size='10'>Gametes</text></svg>

subject: Biology
title: Cancer Biology
description: Uncontrolled cell division. Loss of Contact Inhibition. Metastasis (spread to other organs). Benign (localized) vs Malignant (spreading) tumors.
visual_data:
Carcinogens: UV, Tobacco, X-rays
Genes: Proto-oncogenes (normal) -> Oncogenes (cancer)

subject: Biology
title: Common Bacterial Diseases
description: Typhoid (Salmonella typhi - Widal Test). Pneumonia (Streptococcus pneumoniae - Alveoli fluid). Plague (Yersinia pestis).
visual_data:
Typhoid: High fever, stomach pain, perforation
Pneumonia: Chills, gray/bluish lips/nails

subject: Biology
title: Drugs & Alcohol Abuse
description: Opioids (Heroin/Smack - Depressant). Cannabinoids (Marijuana - Cardiovascular). Coca alkaloids (Coke - Euphoria). Hallucinogens (LSD, Datura).
visual_data:
Cirrhosis: Liver damage from Alcohol
Withdrawal: Anxiety, Shakiness, Nausea

subject: Biology
title: B-Cells vs T-Cells
description: B-Lymphocytes: Produce Antibodies (Humoral Immunity). T-Lymphocytes: Help B-cells and kill infected cells directly (Cell Mediated Immunity - CMI).

subject: Biology
title: Innate Immunity Barriers
description: Physical (Skin, Mucus). Physiological (Acid in stomach, Tears). Cellular (PMNL-Neutrophils, Monocytes, Macrophages). Cytokine (Interferons - anti-viral).
visual_data:
PMNL: Polymorpho-Nuclear Leukocytes
First line of defense (Non-specific)

subject: Biology
title: Ringworm (Fungal)
description: Caused by Microsporum, Trichophyton, Epidermophyton. Symptoms: Dry, scaly lesions, itching. Thrives in heat and moisture (skin folds).
visual_data: Infectious: Transmitted via towels, clothes, combs

subject: Biology
title: Ascariasis
description: Intestinal parasite (Ascaris lumbricoides). Eggs in faeces -> Soil -> Water/Vegetables. Internal bleeding, muscular pain, blockage of intestinal passage.
visual_data:
Prevention: Hygiene, Washing vegetables
Vector-less transmission (Direct)

subject: Biology
title: Elephantiasis (Filariasis)
description: Wuchereria bancrofti / W. malayi. Chronic inflammation of lymphatic vessels (lower limbs). Transmitted by Culex mosquito.
visual_data:
Vector: Culex (Female)
Symptom: Gross deformities of genital organs

subject: Biology
title: Drugs & Sources Summary
description: Morphine (Latex of Poppy). Cannabinoids (Inflorescence of Cannabis). Cocaine (Erythroxylum coca). LSD (Fungus Claviceps).
visual_data:
Tobacco: Nicotine (Stimulates Adrenal gland)
Alcohol: Depressant, affects Cerebellum

subject: Biology
title: Five Antibody Classes
description: The five immunoglobulin classes a NEET student must recall. \(\text{IgG}\)=most abundant, crosses placenta; \(\text{IgA}\)=in colostrum/secretions; \(\text{IgM}\)=largest, first in primary response; \(\text{IgE}\)=allergy/parasites; \(\text{IgD}\)=B-cell surface receptor.

subject: Biology
title: Lymphoid Organs Count
visual_data: \text{Primary: Bone Marrow, Thymus} \\ \text{Secondary: Spleen, Lymph Nodes, Tonsils, Peyer's Patches, Appendix}
description: Classification of lymphoid organs (site of lymphocyte origin vs maturation/interaction). Primary = origin and maturation of lymphocytes; Secondary = sites where lymphocytes interact with antigen and proliferate.

subject: Biology
title: MALT Fraction
description: Mucosa-Associated Lymphoid Tissue constitutes about half of body's lymphoid tissue, lining the respiratory, digestive and urogenital tracts. Frequently asked exact value in NEET.

subject: Biology
title: AIDS Diagnostic Test
description: Standard diagnostic for AIDS. ELISA = enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, the routine screening test; Western blot used for confirmation. PCR detects viral nucleic acid early.

subject: Biology
title: HIV Target Cell
description: HIV primarily attacks helper-T (CD4+) lymphocytes; their progressive decline causes immunodeficiency. Macrophages also act as an HIV reservoir.

subject: Biology
title: Opioid Receptor Site
description: Opioids (heroin/smack, morphine) bind receptors in the central nervous system and gastrointestinal tract; act as depressants slowing body functions. Heroin = diacetylmorphine, white, obtained by acetylation of morphine.

subject: Biology
title: Interferons
description: Interferons are antiviral proteins secreted by virus-infected cells that protect surrounding non-infected cells; part of physiological/innate barrier of immunity.

subject: Biology
title: Primary vs Secondary Response
description: Antibody response on second antigen exposure is far stronger and faster than the first, because of memory B and T cells. Basis of vaccination and immunological memory.

subject: Biology
title: Allergy Mediators
description: Allergic reaction sequence. Allergens trigger IgE-type antibodies; mast cells release histamine and serotonin (chemicals causing allergy symptoms). Anti-histamines used as drugs.

subject: Biology
title: Filariasis Pathogen & Site
description: Lymphatic filariasis (elephantiasis) is caused by Wuchereria bancrofti and W. malayi, which inhabit and chronically block lymphatic vessels, usually of the lower limbs.

subject: Biology
title: Malaria Pathogen & Toxin
description: Malaria caused by Plasmodium (P. vivax, P. malariae, P. falciparum). The toxin haemozoin, released on RBC rupture, causes chill-and-fever; P. falciparum causes the most serious (malignant) malaria.

subject: Biology
title: Common Cold Features
description: Common cold is caused by rhinoviruses; infects nose and upper respiratory tract but not the lungs. Lasts 3-7 days; spread by droplets/contaminated objects.

subject: Biology
title: Amoebiasis Pathogen & Vector
description: Amoebic dysentery caused by Entamoeba histolytica residing in the large intestine; houseflies act as mechanical carriers transmitting the parasite to food.

subject: Biology
title: Pyramid of Numbers
description: Upright in Grassland (Producer > Herbivore > Carnivore). Inverted in Tree ecosystem (Tree < Birds < Parasites).

Cons.</text><text x='100' y='110' text-anchor='middle' font-size='10'>Sec. Cons.</text></svg>

subject: Biology
title: Pyramid of Biomass
description: Usually Upright. Inverted in Aquatic ecosystem (Phytoplankton mass < Zooplankton mass).

subject: Biology
title: Ecological Succession (Xerarch)
description: Succession on bare rock. Lichen (Pioneer) -> Bryophytes -> Herbs -> Shrubs -> Forest (Climax).

subject: Biology
title: Carbon vs Phosphorus Cycle
description: Carbon flows through photosynthesis/respiration. Phosphorus flows through weathering/absorption. No respiratory release of Phosphorus.
derivation: 71% Carbon found in oceans.

subject: Biology
title: Phosphorus Cycle
description: Sedimentary cycle. Reservoir: Rocks. Weathering releases phosphate -> Soil -> Plants -> Animals -> Detritus -> Soil.
visual_data:
Difference from Carbon Cycle:
1. No respiratory release of P
2. Atmospheric input is negligible

subject: Biology
title: Decomposition Steps
description: Breakdown of detritus. 1. Fragmentation (Earthworm). 2. Leaching (Water soluble nutrients go down). 3. Catabolism (Enzymes). 4. Humification. 5. Mineralization.
visual_data:
Detritivores: Earthworms (Farmer's friend)
Factors: Warm/Moist (Fast), Chitin/Lignin rich (Slow)

subject: Biology
title: Stratification
description: Vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels. Example in Forest: Trees (Top) -> Shrubs (Middle) -> Herbs/Grasses (Bottom).
visual_data: <svg viewBox='0 0 100 150' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='20' y='130' width='60' height='20' fill='#A7F3D0'/><text x='50' y='145' text-anchor='middle' font-size='8'>Herbs</text><rect x='20' y='90' width='60' height='40' fill='#34D399'/><text x='50' y='115' text-anchor='middle' font-size='8'>Shrubs</text><rect x='10' y='10' width='80' height='80' fill='#059669'/><text x='50' y='50' text-anchor='middle' font-size='8'>Trees</text></svg>

subject: Biology
title: Food Web vs Chain
description: Food Chain: Linear (Grass -> Goat -> Man). Food Web: Interconnected chains (More stable). GFC (Grazing Food Chain). DFC (Detritus Food Chain).
visual_data: \text{DFC (Decomposers)} \to \text{Major flow in terrestrial ecosystem} \\ \text{GFC} \to \text{Major flow in aquatic ecosystem}

subject: Biology
title: Pyramid of Energy
description: Always Upright. Energy flow is unidirectional. 10% Law (Lindeman): Only 10% energy transferred to next trophic level.

subject: Biology
title: GPP vs NPP
description: Net usable energy available to consumers/heterotrophs. \(GPP\)=Gross Primary Productivity (total organic matter produced in photosynthesis), \(R\)=respiration loss, \(NPP\)=Net Primary Productivity (biomass available for consumption).
derivation: NPP is the basis of the food chain (available to herbivores & decomposers).

subject: Biology
title: 10% Law (Lindeman)
visual_data: \text{Energy at next level} = 10\% \text{ of previous level}
description: Only 10% of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next; ~90% lost as heat/respiration. \(T_1 \to T_2 \to T_3\) gives 1000J \(\to\) 100J \(\to\) 10J. Limits chain to 4-5 trophic levels.
derivation: Energy flow is unidirectional (Sun $\to$ Producer $\to$ Consumers); obeys laws of thermodynamics.

subject: Biology
title: Annual Net Primary Productivity
description: Standard global productivity values for NEET recall. Total annual NPP \(\approx 170\) billion tonnes organic matter. Oceans cover ~70% of surface but contribute only ~55 billion tonnes (low productivity).

subject: Biology
title: Productivity Units
description: Rate of biomass production, expressed per unit area per unit time. Measured as weight \((g\,m^{-2})\) or energy \((kcal\,m^{-2})\). Distinguishes productivity (rate) from standing crop (stock).

subject: Biology
title: Sun's Energy Captured (PAR)
description: Fraction of incident solar energy fixed by producers. Of total incident light, ~50% is Photosynthetically Active Radiation (PAR); plants capture only 2-10% of PAR. Sets the upper limit of all ecosystem energy.

subject: Biology
title: Climax Community (Succession)
description: End-point of ecological succession in equilibrium with environment. Primary succession (bare rock/new area) is very slow; secondary succession (after disturbance, e.g. burnt land) is faster as soil already exists.
derivation: Hydrarch succession (in water) and Xerarch succession (on dry land) both converge toward a mesic (moderate-moisture) climax.

subject: Biology
title: Biomagnification
description: Increase in concentration of toxicant (DDT/Mercury) at successive trophic levels.
visual_data: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='20' y='160' width='160' height='30' fill='#BFDBFE'/><text x='100' y='180' text-anchor='middle' font-size='10'>Water (0.003 ppb)</text><circle cx='100' cy='130' r='15' fill='#FCA5A5'/><text x='140' y='135' font-size='10'>Zoo (0.04 ppm)</text><ellipse cx='100' cy='90' rx='25' ry='15' fill='#F87171'/><text x='150' y='95' font-size='10'>Fish (0.5 ppm)</text><path d='M80,50 L120,50 L100,20 Z' fill='#EF4444'/><text x='150' y='40' font-size='10'>Bird (25 ppm)</text><line x1='100' y1='160' x2='100' y2='60' stroke='#000' stroke-width='2' marker-end='url(#arrow)'/></svg>

subject: Biology
title: Ozone Depletion
description: Good Ozone (Stratosphere) protects from UV-B. Bad Ozone (Troposphere). Thickness measured in Dobson Units (DU). CFCs release Cl atoms which degrade Ozone.
visual_data: CF_2Cl_2 \xrightarrow{UV} Cl \bullet \\ Cl \bullet + O_3 \to ClO + O_2

subject: Biology
title: Greenhouse Gases
description: Contribution to Global Warming. Gases absorb long-wave IR radiation from Earth.
derivation: Kyoto Protocol targets reduction of these gases.

subject: Biology
title: Eutrophication
description: Natural aging of lake by nutrient enrichment (N, P). Cultural Eutrophication (accelerated by humans). Causes Algal Bloom -> O2 depletion -> Fish death.

subject: Biology
title: Solid Waste Management
description: Sanitary Landfills (leachate problem). Incineration (Hospital waste). Recycling (Plastics - Ahmed Khan's Polyblend for roads). E-waste (Gold recovery - Toxic).

subject: Biology
title: Deforestation Case Studies
description: Chipko Movement (1974, Garhwal Himalayas - Sunderlal Bahuguna). Amrita Devi Bishnoi (1731, Rajasthan - sacrificed life for Khejri trees).
visual_data: JFM: Joint Forest Management (1980s) - Local communities protect forests

subject: Biology
title: Protocols
description: Montreal Protocol (1987, Canada): Control ODS (Ozone Depleting Substances - CFCs). Kyoto Protocol (1997, Japan): Control Greenhouse Gases (Climate Change).
visual_data:
Montreal: Ozone protection
Kyoto: Global Warming

subject: Biology
title: Ozone Hole Mechanism
description: Antarctic Region. UV breaks CFCs -> Cl atoms -> Cl converts Ozone to Oxygen. Cl acts as catalyst (not consumed). Thinning of shield.
visual_data: Cl + O_3 \to ClO + O_2 \\ ClO + O \to Cl + O_2

subject: Biology
title: Catalytic Converter Metals
description: Catalytic converter uses expensive metals to convert exhaust pollutants. Pt=platinum, Pd=palladium, Rh=rhodium; converts unburnt hydrocarbons and toxic gases to harmless products. Requires unleaded petrol.

subject: Biology
title: Electrostatic Precipitator
description: ESP removes particulate matter from thermal plant exhaust. Removes over 99% of particulate matter; electrode generates corona that charges particles, collected on grounded plates.

subject: Biology
title: Respirable Particulate Size
description: Particle size most dangerous to human health. PM 2.5=particulate matter of diameter \(\le 2.5\,\mu m\); these fine particles penetrate deep into the lungs and cause respiratory and cardiovascular disorders.

subject: Biology
title: BOD Significance
description: Biochemical Oxygen Demand indicates organic pollution load. BOD=oxygen consumed by microbes to decompose organic matter in a water sample; higher BOD means more pollution and lower dissolved oxygen.

subject: Biology
title: Integrated Waste Treatment (Arcata)
description: Arcata integrated waste-water treatment uses six marsh stages after conventional treatment. Stages 1-2 are conventional sedimentation/filtration; stages 3-6 use marsh plants, algae, fungi and bacteria to neutralize and absorb pollutants/heavy metals.

subject: Biology
title: Chipko Movement
description: Landmark Indian forest conservation movement. Chipko movement of 1974 in the Garhwal Himalayas where local women hugged trees to prevent contractors from cutting them.

subject: Biology
title: Amrita Devi Bishnoi
visual_data: 1731 \text{ AD, Khejarli (Rajasthan)} \\ 363 \text{ people sacrificed for Khejri trees}
description: Historic sacrifice for tree protection; basis of the wildlife protection award. In 1731 AD Amrita Devi Bishnoi led 363 people who died protecting Khejri (Prosopis) trees in Khejarli village, Jodhpur.

subject: Biology
title: Forest Cover Recommendation
description: Balanced forest cover recommended by the National Forest Policy. Of total land, 33% forest cover is recommended for plains and 67% for hilly regions to maintain ecological balance.

subject: Biology
title: Ozone Measurement (Dobson)
description: Unit for measuring stratospheric ozone column. Ozone is measured in Dobson Units (DU); the ozone hole over Antarctica is a region of severely thinned ozone in DU.

subject: Biology
title: UV-B Effects
description: Biological damage from increased UV-B radiation due to ozone depletion. UV-B is absorbed by DNA causing mutations; leads to skin ageing, skin cancer, cataract and inflammation of the cornea (snow-blindness).

subject: Biology
title: Biodiversity Hotspots
description: High species richness and high endemism. 34 globally. India: Western Ghats, Himalayas, Indo-Burma.

subject: Biology
title: Species-Area Curve (Log)
description: Linear on log-log scale. Steeper slope (Z) for larger areas (continents).

subject: Biology
title: In-situ vs Ex-situ
description: In-situ (On site): National Parks, Sanctuaries, Biosphere Reserves, Sacred Groves. Ex-situ (Off site): Zoos, Botanical Gardens, Cryopreservation, Seed Banks.
visual_data:
In-situ: Protect whole ecosystem
Ex-situ: Protect specific endangered species

subject: Biology
title: Evil Quartet (Loss Causes)
visual_data:
1. Habitat Loss & Fragmentation (Most imp)
2. Over-exploitation
3. Alien Species Invasion (Water Hyacinth)
4. Co-extinction

subject: Biology
title: In-situ Conservation
description: On-site. Hotspots (Western Ghats), Biosphere Reserves (14 in India), National Parks (90), Sanctuaries (448), Sacred Groves (Khasi Hills, Aravalli).
visual_data: Sacred Groves: Last refuge for large number of rare plants

subject: Biology
title: Global Species Diversity (IUCN 2004)
description: Standard IUCN figures for number of described species on Earth. Animals dominate; among animals, insects are the single largest group.

subject: Biology
title: Estimated vs Described Species
visual_data: \begin{array}{l} \text{Described} \approx 1.5 \text{ million} \\ \text{Robert May estimate} \approx 7 \text{ million} \\ \therefore > 70\% \text{ still to be discovered} \end{array}
description: Robert May's conservative global estimate vs species actually described. \(\approx 7\) million total estimated.

subject: Biology
title: India's Share of Global Diversity
visual_data: \begin{array}{l} \text{Land area} = 2.4\% \text{ of world} \\ \text{Species share} = 8.1\% \text{ of global} \end{array}
description: India is a mega-diversity nation: holds \(8.1\%\) of global species on only \(2.4\%\) of land area.

subject: Biology
title: India's Species Numbers
visual_data: \begin{array}{l} \text{Total recorded} \approx 45{,}000 \text{ plants} \\ \approx 90{,}000 \text{ animals} \\ \text{Plants} \approx 6\% \text{ of world flora} \\ \text{Animals} \approx 6.5\% \text{ of world fauna} \end{array}
description: Recorded biodiversity in India (plants and animals) and its fraction of the global total.

subject: Biology
title: Latitudinal Gradient (Tropics)
description: Species richness is highest in the tropics and decreases toward the poles. Amazon rainforest is the richest (e.g. >40,000 plant species).

subject: Biology
title: Rivet Popper Hypothesis
visual_data: \begin{array}{l} \text{Species} = \text{rivets of an airplane} \\ \text{Few lost} \rightarrow \text{weakening} \\ \text{Key species lost} \rightarrow \text{collapse} \end{array}
description: Paul Ehrlich's analogy: each species is a rivet; losing rivets (especially key/keystone ones) progressively destabilises the ecosystem (airplane).

subject: Biology
title: Current Extinction Rate
description: Anthropogenic extinctions are 100-1000 times faster than natural background rates; we are in the 6th mass extinction.

subject: Biology
title: Amphibian Vulnerability
visual_data: \begin{array}{l} \text{More than } 15\% \text{ of all species} \\ \text{face threat of extinction} \\ \text{Amphibians: most vulnerable} \end{array}
description: IUCN Red List indication that >15% of described species are threatened; amphibians are the most vulnerable group.

subject: Biology
title: Earth Summit & Convention Dates
visual_data: \begin{array}{l} \text{Rio Earth Summit} = 1992 \\ \text{World Summit (Johannesburg)} = 2002 \\ \text{Pledge: reduce loss rate by 2010} \end{array}
description: Key dates: Convention on Biological Diversity (Rio, 1992) and the 2002 World Summit on Sustainable Development held at Johannesburg.

subject: Biology
title: Ecosystem Productivity (Stability Expt)
visual_data: \begin{array}{l} \text{David Tilman: more species} \\ \rightarrow \text{less year-to-year variation} \\ \rightarrow \text{higher productivity} \\ \text{Stable community resists invasion} \end{array}
description: Tilman's long-term plot experiments: increased species richness gives greater productivity and lower temporal variability (stability).

subject: Biology
title: Menstrual Cycle (Hormones)
description: Day 14: LH Surge (Ovulation). Follicular Phase (Estrogen high). Luteal Phase (Progesterone high, maintains Endometrium).

title: Spermatogenesis vs Oogenesis
description: Comparison of gamete formation. Spermatogenesis is continuous from puberty. Oogenesis halts at Prophase-I and Metaphase-II.

subject: Biology
title: Embryonic Development
description: Zygote -> Morula (8-16 cells) -> Blastocyst (Implants) -> Gastrula (3 Germ layers). Heart forms after 1 month. Limbs/Digits by 2nd month.
visual_data:
1st Month: Heart beat
2nd Month: Limbs/Digits
1st Trimester: Major Organs
5th Month: First Movement / Hair

title: Sperm Structure

derivation: Acrosome is derived from Golgi body.

subject: Biology
title: Follicular Development
description: Primary Follicle -> Secondary -> Tertiary (Antrum fluid cavity) -> Graafian Follicle (mature). Ruptures to release ovum -> Corpus Luteum.

subject: Biology
title: Parturition (Childbirth)
description: Neuroendocrine mechanism. Fetal Ejection Reflex: Signals from fully developed fetus/placenta -> Oxytocin release (Pituitary) -> Uterine Contractions.

subject: Biology
title: Male Reproductive System
description: Testis (Scrotum - low temp). Seminiferous Tubules (Sperm production). Epididymis (Storage). Vas Deferens. Glands: Seminal Vesicle (Fructose), Prostate, Bulbourethral.

subject: Biology
title: Chromosome Number (Gametes)
description: Ploidy and chromosome count in human gametes vs zygote. \(n\)=haploid (23), \(2n\)=diploid (46). Sperm carries X or Y; ovum always X.

subject: Biology
title: Gestation Period
description: Average human gestation length from last menstrual period. Counted as ~9 calendar months / 3 trimesters.

subject: Biology
title: Germ Layers
description: Three primary germ layers formed during gastrulation that give rise to all tissues/organs. Embryo with these = gastrula (triploblastic).

subject: Biology
title: Polar Body Chromosome Set
description: Oogenesis is unequal: cytoplasm conserved in one large ovum; polar bodies are haploid and degenerate. Primary oocyte is 2n; secondary oocyte/ovum is n.

subject: Biology
title: Egg Count Timeline
visual_data: \text{At Birth} \approx 1 \text{ to } 2 \text{ million primary oocytes} \\ \text{At Puberty} \approx 60{,}000 \text{ to } 80{,}000 \\ 1 \text{ ovum released / cycle}
description: Decline in primary oocyte number from birth to puberty in human ovary. Only one ovum is typically ovulated per menstrual cycle.

subject: Biology
title: Menstrual Cycle Duration
description: Standard human menstrual cycle phases. Menstrual flow days 1-5; follicular phase 1-13; ovulation day 14; luteal phase 15-28.

subject: Biology
title: Thyroid Hormones
description: T3, T4 (Thyroxine) - regulate BMR (Basal Metabolic Rate). TCT (Thyrocalcitonin) - lowers blood calcium. Iodine essential.

subject: Biology
title: Pancreatic Hormones
description: Islets of Langerhans. Alpha cells -> Glucagon (Hyperglycemic). Beta cells -> Insulin (Hypoglycemic).

subject: Biology
title: Adrenal Gland Hormones
description: Cortisol: Anti-inflammatory, Gluconeogenesis. Aldosterone: $Na^+$ and Water reabsorption. Adrenaline: Emergency hormone.
derivation: 3 Layers of Cortex: Glomerulosa, Fasciculata, Reticularis.

subject: Biology
title: Hormone Action Mechanism
description: Protein Hormones (Insulin): Bind membrane receptor -> Second messenger (cAMP/Ca++) -> Response. Steroid Hormones (Estrogen): Cross membrane -> Bind intracellular receptor -> Gene expression.
visual_data:
Membrane Bound: Fast, Cascade effect (e.g., FSH)
Intracellular: Slow, regulate DNA (e.g., Cortisol)

subject: Biology
title: Parathyroid Hormone (PTH)
description: Hypercalcemic hormone. Increases blood Ca++ by bone resorption (demineralization) and reabsorption in kidney. Antagonistic to TCT (Thyrocalcitonin).

subject: Biology
title: Pineal Gland
description: Dorsal side of forebrain. Secretes Melatonin. Regulates Diurnal (24-hour) rhythm (Sleep-wake cycle, Body temp).

subject: Biology
title: Growth Hormone Disorders
description: Disorders from over/under-secretion of Growth Hormone (Somatotropin). Hyposecretion in children stunts growth; hypersecretion before epiphyseal closure causes gigantism; hypersecretion in adults thickens bones (acromegaly).

subject: Biology
title: ADH / Diabetes Insipidus
description: Vasopressin (ADH) action on kidney and disorder on deficiency. ADH promotes water reabsorption at distal tubules/collecting ducts (anti-diuresis) and raises BP; its deficiency causes excessive dilute urine (diabetes insipidus). \(ADH\)=antidiuretic hormone.

subject: Biology
title: Hypothalamic Control
description: Hypothalamus regulates the anterior pituitary via releasing and inhibiting hormones (neurohormones). \(GnRH\)=gonadotropin-releasing, \(TRH\)=thyrotropin-releasing, \(CRH\)=corticotropin-releasing hormone; Somatostatin (GHIH) inhibits GH.

subject: Biology
title: Normal Blood Glucose
description: Normal fasting blood glucose level maintained by insulin-glucagon balance. Persistent elevation = hyperglycemia (Diabetes mellitus); marked fall = hypoglycemia. Value in mg per 100 mL (dL) of blood.

subject: Biology
title: Hormone Chemical Classes
visual_data: \begin{aligned} &\text{Peptide/Protein: Insulin, GH, ADH} \\ &\text{Steroid: Cortisol, Estrogen, Testosterone} \\ &\text{Iodothyronine: } T_3, T_4 \\ &\text{Amino-acid deriv.: Adrenaline} \end{aligned}
description: Classification of hormones by chemical nature. Steroid and iodothyronine (thyroid) hormones are lipid-soluble (intracellular receptors); peptide/protein and amine hormones are water-soluble (membrane receptors). \(T_3\)=triiodothyronine, \(T_4\)=thyroxine.

subject: Biology
title: Thyroid Hormone Synthesis
description: Iodine is essential for thyroid hormone synthesis. \(T_4\) (thyroxine, tetra-iodothyronine) is secreted in larger amount but \(T_3\) (triiodothyronine) is the more potent/active form. Dietary iodine deficiency causes goitre.

subject: Biology
title: Testis & Ovary Hormones
description: Gonadal hormones and their sources. Leydig (interstitial) cells secrete androgens (male secondary sex characters, spermatogenesis); ovary secretes estrogen (female secondary sex characters) and progesterone (supports pregnancy, maintains endometrium).

subject: Biology
title: Diabetes Mellitus
description: Prolonged insulin deficiency/resistance raises blood glucose, causing diabetes mellitus. Excess glucose is excreted in urine (glycosuria); fat breakdown produces ketone bodies (ketoacidosis). Distinct from diabetes insipidus (ADH-linked).

subject: Biology
title: Water Potential
description: \(\Psi_w = \Psi_s + \Psi_p\). Water moves from High \(\Psi_w\) (less negative) to Low \(\Psi_w\) (more negative).

subject: Biology
title: Stomatal Apparatus
description: Regulates transpiration and gas exchange. Guard cells (Bean-shaped in Dicots, Dumbbell in Monocots) control opening/closing via Turgor pressure.

description: Apoplast: Cell wall path (Non-living, Fast). Blocked by Casparian Strip. Symplast: Cytoplasm path via Plasmodesmata (Living, Slow).

subject: Biology
title: Cohesion-Tension Theory
description: Dixon & Joly. Water rises in tall trees due to Transpiration Pull. Cohesion (Water-Water), Adhesion (Water-Xylem), Surface Tension.

subject: Biology
title: Guttation
description: Loss of water as liquid droplets from leaf margins (Hydathodes). Caused by Root Pressure (positive pressure) usually at night/early morning.

subject: Biology
title: Imbibition
description: Absorption of water by solids (colloids) causing increase in volume. Seed germination requires imbibition. Heat is released (Heat of Wetting).

title: Plasmolysis

subject: Biology
title: Osmotic Pressure vs Potential
description: Solute (osmotic) potential is numerically equal but opposite in sign to osmotic pressure. \(\Psi_s\)=solute potential (always negative), \(OP\)=osmotic pressure (positive).

subject: Biology
title: Pure Water Potential
description: Reference value: water potential of pure water at standard temp/pressure is zero; adding solute makes it negative. \(\Psi_w\)=water potential.

subject: Biology
title: Root Pressure Magnitude
visual_data: \text{Root Pressure} \approx 1\text{-}2 \text{ atm} \\ \text{(max} \sim 2 \text{ atm, cannot raise tall trees)}
description: Positive hydrostatic pressure developed in xylem due to active ion uptake; too small to account for ascent in tall trees. Measured in atmospheres (atm).

subject: Biology
title: Transpiration Pull Tension
visual_data: \text{Xylem tension} \to \text{up to } -20 \text{ to } -30 \text{ bar} \\ \text{Cohesion-tension lifts water} > 100 \text{ m}
description: Magnitude of negative pressure (tension) generated by transpiration that pulls the water column up tall trees. Tension in bar; height in metres.

subject: Biology
title: Pressure Flow Hypothesis
description: Munch hypothesis for phloem translocation of sugars by bulk/mass flow along a turgor pressure gradient. \(\Psi_p\)=pressure (turgor) potential.

subject: Biology
title: Facilitated Diffusion
description: Transport of polar/large molecules across membrane via proteins, down the concentration gradient without energy expenditure. Distinguish from active transport (uses ATP, against gradient).

subject: Biology
title: Means of Transport Comparison
visual_data: \begin{aligned} &\text{Diffusion: passive, no ATP, down gradient} \\ &\text{Facilitated: passive, no ATP, protein} \\ &\text{Active: ATP used, against gradient} \end{aligned}
description: Summary of the three modes of membrane transport in plants and their energy/gradient requirements. ATP = energy currency.

subject: Biology
title: Guttation Site
visual_data: \text{Hydathodes} \to \text{exude xylem sap (water + minerals)} \\ \text{driven by Root Pressure (night/early morning)}
description: Guttation is loss of liquid water through hydathodes at leaf vein endings, driven by root pressure when transpiration is low. Distinguish from dew (external condensation).

subject: Biology
title: Transpiration Pull Direction
description: Minerals are transported upward along with water in the transpiration (xylem) stream; transpiration aids mineral distribution. Movement is unidirectional (upward) in xylem.

subject: Biology
title: Nitrogen Cycle Steps
description: 1. Fixation (N2 -> NH3). 2. Nitrification (NH3 -> NO2- -> NO3-). 3. Assimilation (Plants). 4. Ammonification (Dead -> NH3). 5. Denitrification (NO3- -> N2).

title: Deficiency Symptoms

Mobile elements (N, K, Mg): Symptoms in Old Leaves
Immobile elements (Ca, S): Symptoms in Young Leaves

subject: Biology
title: Essential Elements Count
description: Standard NEET recall numbers for plant elemental composition. \(>60\)=total elements detectable in plants, \(17\)=number of essential elements (NCERT). Of these, \(C, H, O\) come from air/water; the other \(14\) are mineral nutrients from soil.

subject: Biology
title: Macro vs Micronutrient Cutoff
description: Concentration criterion separating the two nutrient classes. A nutrient required in concentration \(\ge 10\) mmol per kg of dry matter is a macronutrient; below this it is a micronutrient (trace element). Macros: \(C,H,O,N,P,S,K,Ca,Mg\) (9); Micros: \(Fe,Mn,Cu,Zn,B,Mo,Cl,Ni\) (8).

subject: Biology
title: Biological N2 Fixation
description: Nitrogenase-catalysed reduction of dinitrogen to ammonia. \(N_2\)=dinitrogen, \(16\,ATP\)=energy cost per molecule fixed, \(2NH_3\)=ammonia produced, \(H_2\)=obligate hydrogen by-product. Note: 8 electrons + 8 protons, NOT 6.

subject: Biology
title: Criteria for Essentiality
visual_data: \text{Essential element} \iff \text{(1) completes life cycle} \;\land\; \text{(2) part of a metabolite/enzyme}
description: Arnon & Stout (1939) test for an essential element. Element must be (1) absolutely necessary for normal growth and reproduction so the plant completes its life cycle, AND (2) form part of any essential metabolite or be needed for a specific enzyme/reaction; its requirement must be specific and not replaceable.

subject: Biology
title: Elements by Function (4 Roles)
description: Functional classification of essential mineral elements (4 categories). (i) Components of biomolecules / structural (e.g. \(C,H,O,N\)); (ii) energy-related, members of energy-storing or redox compounds (e.g. \(Mg\) in chlorophyll, \(P\) in ATP); (iii) activators/inhibitors of enzymes (e.g. \(Mg^{2+},Zn^{2+},Mo\)); (iv) altering osmotic potential (e.g. \(K^+\) in stomata).

subject: Biology
title: Toxic Concentration Threshold
description: Standard NCERT definition of a toxic mineral concentration. Any concentration of an element in plant tissues that reduces the dry weight of tissues by about \(10\%\) is considered toxic. Toxicity levels differ widely among elements and plants; e.g. excess \(Mn\) competes with \(Fe, Mg\) uptake and inhibits \(Ca\) translocation.

subject: Biology
title: Nitrate Reduction Steps
description: Reduction of absorbed nitrate to ammonia before assimilation. \(NO_3^-\)=nitrate (form absorbed by most plants) reduced to nitrite \(NO_2^-\) by nitrate reductase (a Mo-containing enzyme), then nitrite to ammonium \(NH_4^+\). Overall valence change of N from \(+5\) to \(-3\).

subject: Biology
title: Population Interactions
description: Mutualism (+/+), Competition (-/-), Predation (+/-), Parasitism (+/-), Commensalism (+/0), Amensalism (-/0).

title: Age Pyramids
description: Shape indicates population growth. Triangular = Expanding (Young > Old). Bell = Stable (Young = Old). Urn = Declining (Young < Old).

title: Population Growth Models
description: Exponential: dN/dt = rN (Unlimited resources). Logistic: dN/dt = rN((K-N)/K) (Limited resources, Carrying Capacity K).

subject: Biology
title: Biotic Potential (r)
description: Intrinsic rate of natural increase. Darwinian fitness. High 'r' means organism reproduces quickly (e.g., bacteria, insects).

subject: Biology
title: Population Attributes
description: Birth Rate (Natality). Death Rate (Mortality). Sex Ratio (Males per 1000 Females). Age Distribution (Pre-reproductive, Reproductive, Post-reproductive).

subject: Biology
title: Logistic Growth Equation
description: Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth in a habitat with limited resources (S-shaped/sigmoid curve). \(N\)=population size, \(r\)=intrinsic rate of natural increase, \(K\)=carrying capacity (max population the habitat can support), \(t\)=time.
derivation:
At low \(N\): \((K-N)/K \approx 1\), so growth is nearly exponential.
When \(N = K\): \((K-N)/K = 0 \Rightarrow dN/dt = 0\) (population stabilizes).
When \(N > K\): term is negative, population declines back toward \(K\).

subject: Biology
title: Exponential Growth (Integral Form)
description: Population size after time t under unlimited resources (J-shaped curve), integral solution of \(dN/dt = rN\). \(N_t\)=population at time \(t\), \(N_0\)=initial population, \(r\)=intrinsic rate of natural increase, \(e\)=base of natural log (\(\approx 2.71828\)).

subject: Biology
title: Population Density Measures
description: Ways to express population size; absolute numbers often replaced by relative measures. Examples: % cover/biomass for plants (e.g. banyan), pugmark/fecal pellet counts for tigers, fish caught per trap (relative density). \(N\)=number of individuals.

subject: Biology
title: Carrying Capacity (K)
description: Maximum population size a given habitat can sustain with its limited resources. At \(N=K\) births equal deaths so net growth is zero; the logistic (S-shaped) curve flattens as an asymptote at \(K\). \(N\)=population size, \(K\)=carrying capacity.

subject: Biology
title: Epithelial Tissue Types
description: Squamous (Diffusion - Lungs), Cuboidal (Secretion - Ducts), Columnar (Absorption - Intestine), Ciliated (Movement - Bronchioles).

subject: Biology
title: Cockroach Excretion
description: Tubules lined by glandular and ciliated cells. Absorb nitrogenous waste from hemolymph and convert to uric acid. Hindgut reabsorbs water.

title: Frog Anatomy (Rana tigrina)

subject: Biology
title: Compound Epithelium & Glands

subject: Biology

description: Methanogens (Methanobacterium) produce Biogas (CH4 + CO2) from dung/slurry under anaerobic conditions.

subject: Biology
title: Sewage Treatment
description: Primary (Physical): Filtration/Sedimentation. Secondary (Biological): Aeration tanks (Flocs consume organic matter, reduce BOD) -> Anaerobic Sludge Digester.

subject: Biology
title: Antibiotics
description: Chemical substances produced by microbes to kill others. Penicillin (First antibiotic - Alexander Fleming from Penicillium notatum). Chain & Florey established potential.
visual_data:
Source: Bacteria (Streptomyces), Fungi (Penicillium)
Action: Disupt cell wall synthesis (Bactericidal)

subject: Biology
title: Biocontrol Agents
description: Ladybird (controls Aphids). Dragonfly (controls Mosquitoes). Bacillus thuringiensis (Caterpillars). Trichoderma (Root pathogens). Baculovirus/Nucleopolyhedrovirus (Specific to insects).
visual_data:
IPM: Integrated Pest Management
Avoid chemical pesticides

subject: Biology
title: Bioactive Molecules
description: Cyclosporin A (Immunosuppressant - Trichoderma polysporum). Statins (Cholesterol lowering - Monascus purpureus). Streptokinase (Clot buster - Streptococcus).
visual_data:
Lipase: Detergents (remove oil stains)
Pectinase/Protease: Clear bottled juices
Swiss Cheese: Large holes (CO2) by Propionibacterium

subject: Biology
title: Sewage Treatment Stages
description: Order of municipal sewage treatment. Primary = physical sedimentation; Secondary = biological oxidation by aerobic microbes forming flocs.

subject: Biology
title: Anaerobic Sludge Digestion
description: Fate of secondary-treatment sludge in anaerobic digesters, producing biogas. Gases = methane, hydrogen sulphide, carbon dioxide.

subject: Biology
title: Biogas Composition
description: Predominant gas in biogas (gobar gas) is methane, produced by methanogens. Methanogen = Methanobacterium.

subject: Biology
title: Curd / Lactic Acid Fermentation
description: Curd formation by Lactic Acid Bacteria. LAB = Lactobacillus; coagulates milk protein (casein), also increases vitamin B12.

subject: Biology
title: Bread / Dough Leavening
description: Baker's yeast ferments dough; CO2 puffs the bread (leavening). Saccharomyces cerevisiae = baker's yeast.

subject: Biology
title: Ethanol Fermentation
description: Alcoholic fermentation of glucose by Saccharomyces cerevisiae (brewer's yeast); basis of wine, beer, whisky.

subject: Biology
title: Distilled vs Undistilled Liquor
description: Distinguishes fermented beverages. Distillation concentrates ethanol for hard liquor; fermentation alone gives wine/beer.

subject: Biology
title: Penicillin Source
description: First antibiotic; discovered by Alexander Fleming from the fungus Penicillium notatum (= P. chrysogenum).

subject: Biology
title: Cyclosporin A
description: Bioactive molecule used as immunosuppressant in organ transplants; produced by the fungus Trichoderma polysporum.

subject: Biology
title: Statins
description: Blood-cholesterol-lowering agent produced by the yeast Monascus purpureus; competitively inhibits cholesterol synthesis enzyme.

subject: Biology
title: Citric Acid Producer
description: Organic acid produced industrially by the fungus Aspergillus niger.

subject: Biology
title: Streptokinase
description: Clot-dissolving enzyme produced by Streptococcus (genetically engineered); used to clear coronary blood clots.

subject: Biology
title: Toddy Fermentation
description: Traditional South-Indian alcoholic drink made by fermenting sap from palms.

subject: Biology
title: Cheese Ripening (Roquefort)
description: Specific cheese flavours from fungal ripening: Roquefort by P. roqueforti, Camembert (soft) by P. camemberti.

subject: Biology
title: Free-living N-fixing Microbes
description: Biofertilisers that fix atmospheric N2 free in soil/water. Aerobic = Azotobacter; anaerobic = Clostridium; algal = Nostoc/Anabaena.

subject: Biology
title: Symbiotic N-fixers
description: Biofertilisers fixing N2 in symbiosis. Rhizobium in legume nodules; Frankia in non-leguminous tree roots.

subject: Biology
title: Mycorrhiza (Glomus)
description: Symbiotic fungus-root association biofertiliser; Glomus genus enhances phosphorus uptake and drought resistance.

subject: Biology
title: Bt / Bacillus thuringiensis
description: Microbial biocontrol agent; spores carry insecticidal Cry protein toxic to caterpillars of butterflies/moths.

subject: Biology
title: Baculovirus Biocontrol
description: Species-specific narrow-spectrum insect/arthropod pathogen used as biocontrol; ideal for IPM, no effect on non-target species.

subject: Biology
title: Trichoderma & Ladybird / Dragonfly
description: Common biocontrol agents: free-living fungus Trichoderma against plant pathogens; beetles/dragonflies as predatory biocontrol.

subject: Biology
title: BOD Principle
description: Biochemical Oxygen Demand = amount of O2 consumed if all organic matter in 1 L water is oxidised by bacteria; higher BOD = more polluted.

subject: Biology
title: Sigmoid Growth Curve
description: Lag Phase (Slow), Log/Exponential Phase (Rapid), Stationary Phase (Limited resources).
visual_data: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 150' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='20' y1='130' x2='180' y2='130' stroke='#000'/><line x1='20' y1='10' x2='20' y2='130' stroke='#000'/><path d='M20,130 Q100,130 120,60 T180,20' fill='none' stroke='#10B981' stroke-width='2'/><text x='100' y='145' font-size='10'>Time</text><text x='5' y='70' font-size='10' transform='rotate(-90 5,70)'>Size/Weight</text><text x='60' y='110' font-size='10' fill='#059669'>Lag</text><text x='100' y='80' font-size='10' fill='#059669'>Log</text><text x='150' y='30' font-size='10' fill='#059669'>Stationary</text></svg>

subject: Biology
title: Plant Hormones Functions
description: Auxin (Apical Dominance, Rooting). Gibberellin (Bolting, Internode elongation). Cytokinin (Cell division, Delay senescence). Ethylene (Ripening). ABA (Stress hormone, Stomata closure).
visual_data:
Auxin: Apical Dominance
Gibberellin: 'Bolting' (Sugarcane)
Cytokinin: Cell Division
Ethylene: Fruit Ripening
ABA: Stress / Dormancy

subject: Biology
title: Photoperiodism
description: Response to day length. LDP (Long Day): Flower when day > critical (Wheat). SDP (Short Day): Flower when day < critical (Tobacco). Day Neutral (Tomato).
visual_data: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 100' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='20' y='20' width='60' height='20' fill='#FDE68A' stroke='#000'/><text x='50' y='35' text-anchor='middle' font-size='8'>Light</text><rect x='80' y='20' width='100' height='20' fill='#4B5563' stroke='#000'/><text x='130' y='35' text-anchor='middle' font-size='8' fill='#fff'>Dark (Critical)</text><text x='100' y='60' text-anchor='middle' font-size='10'>SDP requires long dark period</text></svg>

subject: Biology
title: Vernalization
description: Flowering dependent on exposure to low temperature. Prevents precocious reproductive development. Winter varieties (Wheat/Barley) planted in autumn.
visual_data:
Promotes flowering in Biennials:
Cabbage, Sugarbeet, Carrot

subject: Biology
title: Absolute vs Relative Growth
description: Absolute: Total growth per unit time. Relative: Growth per unit initial parameter. (Leaf A 5->10cm vs Leaf B 50->55cm. Absolute same, Relative A > B).

subject: Biology
title: Growth Rate (GR)
visual_data: GR = \frac{\text{Increase in size}}{\text{Unit time}} = \frac{\Delta L}{\Delta t}
description: Growth measured as increase in size per unit time (linear or geometric). \(\Delta L\)=increase in growth parameter (length/area/volume/weight), \(\Delta t\)=time interval.

subject: Biology
title: Arithmetic Growth Rate
description: Linear growth where only one daughter cell divides after mitosis; gives a linear (straight-line) plot. \(L_t\)=length at time \(t\), \(L_0\)=initial length, \(r\)=growth rate (elongation per unit time), \(t\)=time.

subject: Biology
title: Geometric Growth (Exponential)
description: Exponential growth where both daughter cells divide; gives the early log phase of sigmoid curve. \(W_t\)=final size, \(W_0\)=initial size, \(r\)=relative growth rate (efficiency index), \(t\)=time, \(e\)=base of natural log.

subject: Biology
title: Auxin : Cytokinin Ratio (Tissue Culture)
description: Skoog & Miller's classic result: organ differentiation in tissue culture is controlled by the auxin-to-cytokinin ratio, not the absolute amount.

subject: Biology
title: Number of Plant Growth Regulators (PGRs)
visual_data: 5 \text{ major groups: } \text{Auxin, GA, Cytokinin, Ethylene, ABA}
description: PGRs grouped as growth promoters (Auxins, Gibberellins, Cytokinins) and growth inhibitors (ABA, Ethylene). Ethylene is the only gaseous hormone.

subject: Biology
title: First Isolated PGRs / Discovery Facts
visual_data: \begin{aligned} \text{Auxin (IAA)} &\rightarrow \text{Tip of grass coleoptile} \\ \text{GA}_3 &\rightarrow \textit{Gibberella fujikuroi} \\ \text{Cytokinin (Kinetin)} &\rightarrow \text{Herring sperm DNA} \end{aligned}
description: Standard NEET discovery/source facts. GA3 (gibberellic acid) is the most studied gibberellin; kinetin and zeatin (from corn-kernel/maize) are natural cytokinins.

subject: Biology
title: C/N Ratio and Flowering
description: High carbohydrate-to-nitrogen ratio promotes flowering/reproductive phase; low C/N (high N) favours vegetative growth. \(C\)=carbohydrate, \(N\)=nitrogen.

subject: Biology
title: Differentiation, Dedifferentiation, Redifferentiation
description: Sequence of maturation in plants. Dedifferentiation = mature cells regain division capacity (e.g. interfascicular cambium, cork cambium); redifferentiation = these again lose it to form secondary tissues.

subject: Biology
title: Plasticity (Heterophylly Example)
description: Plasticity = different growth pathways/forms in response to environment or developmental stage. Heterophylly in cotton/coriander (juvenile vs adult) and in aquatic Buttercup (submerged vs aerial leaves).

subject: Biology
title: Seed Viability / Germination Percent
description: Standard quantitative measure of seed viability used in seed technology. Numerator = seeds that germinated, denominator = total seeds tested.

subject: Biology
title: Insulin Maturation
description: Pro-insulin contains A, B, and C peptide chains. Mature Insulin has only A and B chains linked by Disulfide bridges (C-peptide removed).
visual_data: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path d='M50,40 L150,40' fill='none' stroke='#3B82F6' stroke-width='4'/><text x='20' y='45' font-size='10' fill='#3B82F6'>Chain A</text><path d='M50,80 L150,80' fill='none' stroke='#10B981' stroke-width='4'/><text x='20' y='85' font-size='10' fill='#10B981'>Chain B</text><line x1='70' y1='40' x2='70' y2='80' stroke='#F59E0B' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='120' y1='40' x2='120' y2='80' stroke='#F59E0B' stroke-width='2'/><text x='95' y='65' font-size='8' fill='#F59E0B'>S-S</text><path d='M150,40 Q180,60 150,80' fill='none' stroke='#9CA3AF' stroke-width='2' stroke-dasharray='4,2'/><text x='170' y='60' font-size='8' fill='#9CA3AF'>C-Peptide</text></svg>

subject: Biology
title: Bt Cotton Mechanism
description: Bacillus thuringiensis. Toxin binds to midgut epithelium of insect $\to$ Lysis $\to$ Death. CryIAc (Bollworm), CryIAb (Corn borer).
derivation: Specific to Lepidopterans, Coleopterans, Dipterans.

subject: Biology
title: Genetically Engineered Insulin
visual_data: \text{Eli Lilly (1983)}: \text{Chain A and B produced separately in E. coli} \to \text{Combined via Disulfide bonds}
description: Overcame problem of C-peptide removal. Trade name: Humulin.
derivation: Recombinant DNA technology application.

subject: Biology
title: RNA Interference (RNAi)
description: Gene silencing defense in eukaryotes. dsRNA binds to mRNA and destroys it, preventing translation. Used in nematode resistant tobacco (Meloidegyne incognita).

subject: Biology
title: Ethical Issues (GEAC)
description: GEAC (Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee). Validates GM research and safety of releasing GM organisms. Biopiracy: Theft of bio-resources (e.g., Basmati rice patent).
visual_data:
Functions of GEAC:
1. Safety of GM crops
2. Field trials approval
3. Environmental impact assessment

subject: Biology
title: ELISA
description: Enzyme Linked Immuno-Sorbent Assay. Diagnostic test for AIDS/STDs. Based on Antigen-Antibody interaction.

subject: Biology
title: Applications of PCR
description: Early diagnosis of pathogens (Detects low concentration). HIV in suspected AIDS. Genetic mutations in Cancer. DNA Fingerprinting.

subject: Biology
title: Transgenic Animals
description: Rosie (First Transgenic Cow - Human alpha-lactalbumin enriched milk, 2.4g/L). Mice (Polio vaccine safety). Sheep (Tracey - alpha-1-antitrypsin for Emphysema).

subject: Biology
title: Golden Rice Trait
description: Transgenic rice engineered to combat Vitamin A deficiency. Endosperm accumulates \(\beta\)-carotene (provitamin A), giving the golden color.

subject: Biology
title: First Gene Therapy
description: First clinical gene therapy was for Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency causing SCID, performed in 1990. Functional ADA cDNA introduced into patient's lymphocytes.

subject: Biology
title: Rosie - First Transgenic Cow
description: First transgenic cow Rosie produced human protein-enriched milk containing human alpha-lactalbumin at 2.4 g per litre, more nutritionally balanced for human babies.

subject: Biology
title: Eli Lilly Insulin Chains
description: Human insulin polypeptide lengths. A chain has 21 amino acids, B chain has 30 amino acids, linked by disulfide bridges.

subject: Biology
title: Enzyme Inhibition Types
description: Competitive: Inhibitor mimics substrate, binds Active Site (\(V_{max}\) same, \(K_m\) increases). Non-competitive: Binds Allosteric Site (\(V_{max}\) decreases).
visual_data: \text{Comp: } K_m \uparrow, V_{max} \text{ same} \\ \text{Non-Comp: } V_{max} \downarrow, K_m \text{ same}

subject: Biology
title: Bonds in DNA
visual_data: \text{N-Glycosidic: Sugar + Base} \\ \text{Phosphodiester: Sugar + Phosphate (Backbone)} \\ \text{Hydrogen: Base + Base}
description: Nucleoside = Sugar + Base. Nucleotide = Nucleoside + Phosphate.
derivation: Directionality 5' (Phosphate) to 3' (OH).

subject: Biology
title: Michaelis-Menten Graph
description: Hyperbolic curve. Vmax = Max velocity. Km = Substrate concentration at Vmax/2. Low Km = High Affinity.
visual_data: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 150' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='20' y1='130' x2='180' y2='130' stroke='#000'/><line x1='20' y1='10' x2='20' y2='130' stroke='#000'/><path d='M20,130 Q40,30 180,30' fill='none' stroke='#3B82F6' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='20' y1='30' x2='180' y2='30' stroke='#000' stroke-dasharray='4,2'/><text x='10' y='30' font-size='10'>Vmax</text><line x1='20' y1='80' x2='60' y2='80' stroke='#000' stroke-dasharray='4,2'/><text x='10' y='80' font-size='10'>Vmax/2</text><line x1='60' y1='80' x2='60' y2='130' stroke='#000' stroke-dasharray='4,2'/><text x='60' y='145' font-size='10'>Km</text></svg>

subject: Biology
title: Lipid Structure
description: Fatty Acids (R-COOH) + Glycerol (Tri-hydroxy propane). Triglyceride = 1 Glycerol + 3 Fatty Acids (Ester bond). Saturated (No double bond), Unsaturated (Double bond).
visual_data: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 100' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='20' y='20' width='20' height='60' fill='#BFDBFE'/><text x='30' y='55' text-anchor='middle' font-size='8' transform='rotate(-90 30,55)'>Glycerol</text><rect x='50' y='25' width='100' height='10' fill='#FCA5A5'/><rect x='50' y='45' width='100' height='10' fill='#FCA5A5'/><rect x='50' y='65' width='100' height='10' fill='#FCA5A5'/><text x='100' y='33' text-anchor='middle' font-size='8'>Fatty Acid</text><text x='100' y='53' text-anchor='middle' font-size='8'>Fatty Acid</text><text x='100' y='73' text-anchor='middle' font-size='8'>Fatty Acid</text><line x1='40' y1='30' x2='50' y2='30' stroke='#000'/><line x1='40' y1='50' x2='50' y2='50' stroke='#000'/><line x1='40' y1='70' x2='50' y2='70' stroke='#000'/></svg>

subject: Biology
title: Protein Structure Levels
description: Primary (Sequence of AA). Secondary (Helix/Sheet - H-bonds). Tertiary (3D folding - Disulfide/Ionic bonds - Active form). Quaternary (Multiple polypeptides - Hb).

subject: Biology
title: Enzyme Co-factors
description: Non-protein part essential for activity. Prosthetic Group (Tightly bound - Haem in Peroxidase). Co-enzyme (Transient - NAD/NADP). Metal Ions (Zn in Carboxypeptidase).

subject: Biology
title: Peptide Bond Count
description: Bonds formed when \(n\) amino acids polymerise into one linear polypeptide. Each peptide bond forms by dehydration (loss of one water).

subject: Biology
title: Standard Amino Acids
visual_data: \text{Amino acids in proteins} = 20 \\ \text{Essential} = 9 \quad (\text{e.g. Val, Leu, Lys})
description: Count of amino acids used to build proteins. 20 are protein-forming; 9 are essential (must be obtained from diet).

subject: Biology
title: Enzyme Q10 Value
visual_data: Q_{10} = \frac{\text{Rate at } (T+10)^\circ C}{\text{Rate at } T^\circ C} \approx 2
description: Temperature coefficient of enzyme/metabolic reactions. Reaction rate roughly doubles for every \(10^\circ C\) rise (within the working range, up to the optimum).

subject: Biology
title: Activation Energy Lowering
visual_data: E + S \rightleftharpoons ES \rightarrow E + P \\ \Delta G^{\ddagger}_{\text{enzyme}} < \Delta G^{\ddagger}_{\text{uncatalysed}}
description: Enzyme mechanism: a transient enzyme-substrate (ES) complex lowers the activation energy. Enzymes speed reaction without altering net \(\Delta G\) or equilibrium; \(\Delta G^{\ddagger}\)=activation energy.

subject: Biology
title: Polysaccharide Linkages
description: Glycosidic bond types in storage and structural polysaccharides. All are glucose polymers; the bond type (\(\alpha\) vs \(\beta\)) determines digestibility and structure.

subject: Biology
title: Nucleotide Components
description: Building blocks of nucleic acids. A nucleotide is a nucleoside plus a phosphate group; the sugar is ribose (RNA) or deoxyribose (DNA).

subject: Biology
title: Plant Life Cycles
description: Haplontic (Volvox, Spirogyra). Diplontic (Fucus, Gymnosperms, Angiosperms). Haplo-diplontic (Bryophytes, Pteridophytes).
visual_data:
Haplontic: Zygotic Meiosis (Algae)
Diplontic: Gametic Meiosis (Seed plants)
Haplo-diplontic: Alternation of Gen.

subject: Biology
title: Algae Classification
visual_data: \begin{array}{l|l|l} \text{Class} & \text{Pigments} & \text{Food} \\ \hline \text{Chlorophyceae} & \text{Chl a, b} & \text{Starch} \\ \text{Phaeophyceae} & \text{Chl a, c, Fucoxanthin} & \text{Mannitol} \\ \text{Rhodophyceae} & \text{Chl a, d, Phycoerythrin} & \text{Floridean} \end{array}
description: Green (Volvox), Brown (Fucus, Kelp), Red (Polysiphonia). Brown algae have Algin coating. Red algae produce Agar.
derivation: Pigment depth penetration: Red algae found deepest (absorb blue light).

subject: Biology
title: Bryophytes (Amphibians of Plant Kingdom)
description: Liverworts (Marchantia) & Mosses (Funaria). Depend on water for fertilization. Dominant phase: Gametophyte (n). Sporophyte depends on Gametophyte.
visual_data: <svg viewBox='0 0 100 150' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path d='M50,140 Q20,120 10,100 Q30,120 50,130 Q70,120 90,100 Q80,120 50,140' fill='#10B981' stroke='#064E3B'/><text x='50' y='145' text-anchor='middle' font-size='8'>Gametophyte (n)</text><line x1='50' y1='130' x2='50' y2='50' stroke='#F59E0B' stroke-width='2'/><text x='60' y='90' font-size='8'>Seta</text><ellipse cx='50' cy='40' rx='10' ry='15' fill='#F59E0B'/><text x='50' y='20' text-anchor='middle' font-size='8'>Capsule (2n)</text></svg>

subject: Biology
title: Pteridophytes (Ferns)
description: First terrestrial vascular plants (Xylem/Phloem). Dominant phase: Sporophyte (2n). Gametophyte (Prothallus) is small, free-living, photosynthetic.
visual_data:
Examples: Selaginella, Equisetum
Spores: Homosporous (Similiar) or Heterosporous (Different - Selaginella)

subject: Biology
title: 5 Algal Classes (NCERT)
description: Standard class-count of Algae and their reserve food. Diatoms (Bacillariophyceae) under Chrysophyceae; cell wall has silica.

related_concepts.name: Diatomaceous earth
related_concepts.definition: Indestructible silica-walls of diatoms accumulate to form 'diatomite', used in polishing & filtration.

subject: Biology
title: Chromosome Number per Generation
description: Which generation is dominant (free-living) and its ploidy across plant groups. \(n\)=haploid gametophyte, \(2n\)=diploid sporophyte.

subject: Biology
title: Angiosperm Endosperm Ploidy
description: Double fertilization products in angiosperms. Triple fusion = 2 polar nuclei + 1 male gamete giving triploid \(3n\) endosperm; syngamy = egg + male gamete giving \(2n\) zygote.

subject: Biology
title: Monocot vs Dicot Numbers
description: Key counting differences between the two angiosperm classes. Floral parts in multiples of 3 (trimerous) vs 4/5 (tetra/pentamerous).

subject: Biology
title: Chordata Characteristics
description: 1. Notochord. 2. Dorsal hollow nerve cord. 3. Paired pharyngeal gill slits. 4. Post-anal tail. Closed circulatory system.
visual_data:
Fundamental Features:
1. Notochord (Rod-like)
2. Nerve Cord (Dorsal, Hollow)
3. Gill Slits (Pharyngeal)
4. Post-anal Tail

subject: Biology
title: Phyla Features Summary
visual_data: \begin{array}{l} \text{Porifera: Cellular, Choanocytes} \\ \text{Cnidaria: Tissue, Cnidoblasts} \\ \text{Platyhelminthes: Acoelomate, Flame Cells} \\ \text{Arthropoda: Jointed legs, Chitin} \end{array}
description: Key distinguishing features. Annelida (Metamerism), Mollusca (Radula/Mantle), Echinodermata (Water Vascular System).
derivation: Evolutionary trend: Cellular $\to$ Tissue $\to$ Organ $\to$ Organ System.

subject: Biology
title: Cnidoblast Structure
description: Characteristic of Coelenterata (Cnidaria). Stinging cell for defense/prey. Contains nematocyst (capsule with toxin).
visual_data:
Function: Anchorage, Defense, Capture of Prey
Example: Hydra, Jellyfish, Sea Anemone

subject: Biology
title: Aschelminthes (Roundworms)
description: Pseudocoelomates (False body cavity). Bilateral symmetry. Muscular pharynx. Sexual dimorphism (Males shorter than Females).

subject: Biology
title: Mollusca Features
description: Soft bodied, Calcareous shell. Body: Head, Muscular Foot, Visceral Hump. Mantle cavity (respiration/excretion). Radula (Rasping organ for feeding).
visual_data:
Examples: Pila (Apple Snail), Octopus (Devil fish)
2nd Largest Phylum (after Arthropoda)

subject: Biology
title: Class Pisces (Fishes)
description: Chondrichthyes (Cartilaginous - Shark/Scoliodon, Placoid scales, No Air bladder). Osteichthyes (Bony - Rohu/Labeo, Cycloid scales, Air bladder present).
visual_data:
Chondrichthyes: Mouth ventral, Gill slits separate (no operculum)
Osteichthyes: Mouth terminal, 4 pairs gills (with operculum)

subject: Biology
title: Class Amphibia
description: Dual life (Land + Water). 3-chambered heart (2 Auricles, 1 Ventricle). Respiration: Skin (Cutaneous), Lungs (Pulmonary), Gills (Larva).
visual_data:
Example: Rana (Frog), Bufo (Toad), Salamandra
Tympanum represents ear. Cloaca present.

subject: Biology
title: Class Reptilia
description: Creeping/Crawling mode. Dry cornified skin (Scales/Scutes). 3-chambered heart (4 in Crocodile). Cold-blooded (Poikilotherms).
visual_data:
Example: Chelone (Turtle), Naja (Cobra), Hemidactylus (Lizard)
Snake/Lizard shed skin as cast.

subject: Biology
title: Class Aves (Birds)
description: Feathers, Beak, Forelimbs modified to Wings. Pneumatic bones (Hollow). 4-chambered heart. Warm-blooded (Homeotherms). Double respiration (Air sacs).
visual_data:
Example: Corvus (Crow), Pavo (Peacock)
Digestive tract has Crop and Gizzard.

subject: Biology
title: Class Mammalia
description: Mammary glands (Milk). Hair on skin. External ear (Pinna). 4-chambered heart. Diaphragm. Mostly viviparous (Platypus is oviparous).

subject: Biology
title: Phylum Arthropoda
description: Largest Phylum (2/3rd of all species). Jointed appendages. Chitinous exoskeleton. Molting (Ecdysis). Open circulatory system. Malpighian tubules.
visual_data:
Economical: Apis (Honey), Bombyx (Silk), Laccifer (Lac)
Vectors: Anopheles, Culex, Aedes
Living Fossil: Limulus (King Crab)

subject: Biology
title: Phylum Echinodermata
description: Spiny bodied. Endoskeleton of calcareous ossicles. Marine only. Water Vascular System (Locomotion, Respiration, Food capture).
visual_data:
Symmetry: Radial (Adult), Bilateral (Larva)
Ex: Asterias (Star fish), Echinus (Sea urchin)

subject: Biology
title: Phylum Hemichordata
description: Worm-like marine animals. Stomochord (rudimentary structure). Body: Proboscis, Collar, Trunk. Respiration by gills.
visual_data:
Ex: Balanoglossus, Saccoglossus
Connecting link between Non-chordates and Chordates

subject: Biology
title: Phylum Porifera (Sponges)
description: Primitive, multicellular, cellular level of organization. Water Canal System (Ostia -> Spongocoel -> Osculum). Choanocytes (Collar cells).
visual_data:
Skeleton: Spicules/Spongin fibers
Examples: Sycon, Spongilla (Freshwater), Euspongia (Bath sponge)

subject: Biology
title: Phylum Ctenophora (Sea Walnuts)
description: Marine, Radial symmetry, Diploblastic. 8 external rows of ciliated Comb Plates (Locomotion). Bioluminescence (emit light).

subject: Biology
title: Phylum Platyhelminthes (Flatworms)
description: Dorso-ventrally flattened. Acoelomate. Bilateral symmetry. Flame cells (Osmoregulation/Excretion). Hooks and Suckers in parasites.
visual_data:
Example: Taenia (Tapeworm), Fasciola (Liver fluke)
Regeneration: Planaria (High capacity)

subject: Biology
title: Phylum Annelida (Ringed Worms)
description: Metamerism (Segmentation). Coelomate. Nephridia (Excretion). Longitudinal and Circular muscles (Locomotion). Closed circulatory system.

subject: Biology
title: Heart Chambers in Vertebrates
visual_data: \begin{array}{l} \text{Pisces: 2 chambered} \\ \text{Amphibia: 3 chambered} \\ \text{Reptilia: 3 (4 in Crocodile)} \\ \text{Aves: 4 chambered} \\ \text{Mammalia: 4 chambered} \end{array}
description: Standard count of heart chambers across vertebrate classes, a very high-yield NEET fact. Crocodile is the exception among reptiles with a 4-chambered heart.

subject: Biology
title: Germ Layers (Diploblastic vs Triploblastic)
visual_data: \begin{array}{l} \text{Diploblastic: 2 layers (Ectoderm + Endoderm)} \\ \text{Triploblastic: 3 layers (+ Mesoderm)} \\ \text{Diploblastic: Porifera, Cnidaria, Ctenophora} \end{array}
description: Classification by number of embryonic germ layers. Diploblastic have ectoderm and endoderm with mesoglea between; triploblastic add a true mesoderm (Platyhelminthes onward).

subject: Biology
title: Coelom Classification
visual_data: \begin{array}{l} \text{Acoelomate: no body cavity (Platyhelminthes)} \\ \text{Pseudocoelomate: cavity not mesoderm-lined (Aschelminthes)} \\ \text{Coelomate: true mesoderm-lined cavity (Annelida onward)} \end{array}
description: Classification by presence and nature of body cavity (coelom). A true coelom is lined on both sides by mesoderm; in pseudocoelomates mesoderm is scattered pouches.

subject: Biology
title: Levels of Organisation
description: Increasing grade of body organisation used to classify phyla. Cellular = Porifera; Tissue = Cnidaria/Ctenophora; Organ = Platyhelminthes; Organ-system = Aschelminthes onward.

subject: Biology
title: Body Temperature Regulation
description: Classification of vertebrates by ability to regulate internal body temperature. Only birds and mammals maintain a constant body temperature (homeothermy).

subject: Biology
title: Notochord Basis (Chordata vs Non-chordata)
visual_data: \begin{array}{l} \text{Chordata: notochord present} \\ \text{Non-chordata: notochord absent} \\ \text{Subphyla: Urochordata, Cephalochordata, Vertebrata} \end{array}
description: Primary split of Animalia by presence of notochord. Chordata is divided into 3 subphyla; in vertebrates the notochord is replaced by a vertebral column.

subject: Biology
title: Secondary Growth (Dicot Stem)
description: Vascular Cambium cuts off Secondary Xylem (inside) and Secondary Phloem (outside). Cork Cambium forms Periderm (Bark).

subject: Biology
title: Xylem vs Phloem
visual_data: \text{Xylem (Water)}: \text{Tracheids, Vessels, Fibres, Parenchyma} \\ \text{Phloem (Food)}: \text{Sieve Tubes, Companion Cells, Fibres, Parenchyma}
description: Complex permanent tissues. Xylem is mostly dead (except Parenchyma). Phloem is mostly living (except Fibres). Gymnosperms lack Vessels.
derivation: Companion cells control Sieve tubes (which lack nucleus).

subject: Biology
title: Vascular Bundles
description: Radial (Roots). Conjoint (Stems/Leaves). Open (Cambium present - Dicots). Closed (No Cambium - Monocots).
visual_data: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 100' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><circle cx='50' cy='50' r='40' fill='none' stroke='#000'/><path d='M20,50 L80,50' stroke='#000'/><rect x='30' y='45' width='40' height='10' fill='#EF4444'/><text x='50' y='30' text-anchor='middle' font-size='8'>Phloem</text><text x='50' y='50' text-anchor='middle' font-size='8' fill='#fff'>Cambium</text><text x='50' y='80' text-anchor='middle' font-size='8'>Xylem</text><text x='50' y='95' text-anchor='middle' font-size='8'>Conjoint Open (Dicot)</text></svg>

subject: Biology
title: Secondary Growth in Root
description: Vascular cambium originates from tissue below phloem and Protoxylem. Forms a wavy ring which later becomes circular.
visual_data: \text{Dicots only (No sec growth in Monocots)} \\ \text{Cambium} \to \text{Sec Xylem (In) + Sec Phloem (Out)}

subject: Biology
title: Dorsiventral vs Isobilateral Leaf
description: Dicot (Dorsiventral): Stomata mostly on lower surface, Mesophyll differentiated (Palisade + Spongy). Monocot (Isobilateral): Stomata on both surfaces, Mesophyll undifferentiated.
