subject: Biology
title: Bulliform Cells
description: Large, empty, colorless cells in epidermis of Grasses (Monocots). When turgid -> Leaf open. When flaccid (water stress) -> Leaf curls to reduce water loss.

subject: Biology
title: Simple Permanent Tissues
description: Parenchyma (Storage, Photosynthesis - Living). Collenchyma (Mechanical support in young stems - Living, thickened corners). Sclerenchyma (Dead, lignified - Fibres/Sclereids).
visual_data:
Collenchyma: Thickened with Cellulose/Pectin
Sclerenchyma: Thickened with Lignin (Nuts, Pulp of Guava)

subject: Biology
title: Casparian Strips
visual_data: \text{Endodermis (Innermost Cortex Layer)} \\ \text{Casparian Strips} = \text{Suberin Deposits} \\ \text{Function} \to \text{Block apoplastic water flow}
description: Identifies the endodermal water-regulating band. Casparian strips are suberin (and lignin) thickenings on radial/tangential walls of the single-layered endodermis controlling water/ion entry into the stele.

subject: Biology
title: Pith in Roots
visual_data: \begin{aligned} &\text{Dicot Root: Pith absent / very small} \\ &\text{Monocot Root: Pith large, well developed} \end{aligned}
description: High-yield distinguishing fact. Large central pith = monocot root; small or absent pith = dicot root (xylem reaches centre).

subject: Biology
title: Apical Meristem Zones
description: Order of growth regions behind the root cap. Cells divide in the meristematic zone, enlarge in elongation, and differentiate (root hairs) in the maturation zone.

subject: Biology
title: Annual Rings
visual_data: \text{1 Annual Ring} = \text{Early(Spring) Wood} + \text{Late(Autumn) Wood} \\ \text{Age of Tree} = \text{No. of Annual Rings}
description: Basis of dendrochronology. One annual ring = one year's spring wood (wide vessels, light) + autumn wood (narrow vessels, dark); ring count estimates tree age.

subject: Biology
title: Heartwood vs Sapwood
visual_data: \begin{aligned} &\text{Heartwood (Duramen): inner, dark, dead, non-conducting} \\ &\text{Sapwood (Alburnum): outer, light, conducting} \end{aligned}
description: Two functional regions of secondary xylem. Heartwood is the inner dead wood filled with tannins/resins (tylose); sapwood is the outer living water-conducting wood.

subject: Biology
title: Cork Cambium Products
description: Defines the periderm and bark. Phellogen cuts cork (phellem) outside and phelloderm inside; periderm = phellem + phellogen + phelloderm. Bark = all tissues outside vascular cambium.

subject: Biology
title: Guard Cells Shape
visual_data: \begin{aligned} &\text{Dicots: Bean / Kidney shaped guard cells} \\ &\text{Grasses (Monocots): Dumb-bell shaped} \end{aligned}
description: Stomatal apparatus identification. Bean-shaped guard cells = dicots; dumb-bell-shaped guard cells = grasses/monocots; inner wall thicker than outer.

subject: Biology
title: Three Tissue Systems
visual_data: \begin{aligned} &1.\ \text{Epidermal (Epidermis, Stomata, Trichomes)} \\ &2.\ \text{Ground (Cortex, Pith, Pericycle, etc.)} \\ &3.\ \text{Vascular (Xylem + Phloem)} \end{aligned}
description: Master classification of plant tissue systems. All cells except vascular bundles in ground tissue constitute the ground tissue system.

subject: Biology
title: Meristem Classification
visual_data: \begin{aligned} &\text{Apical} \to \text{Length (Primary Growth)} \\ &\text{Intercalary} \to \text{at base of internodes/leaves} \\ &\text{Lateral} \to \text{Girth (Sec. Growth: VC + CC)} \end{aligned}
description: Position-based meristem types. Apical + intercalary are primary meristems (elongation); lateral meristems (vascular cambium, cork cambium) cause increase in thickness.

subject: Biology
title: Bundle Sheath / Kranz
visual_data: \text{Monocot Vascular Bundle} \to \text{Bundle Sheath (Sclerenchyma)} \\ \text{Maize Leaf} \to \text{Kranz Anatomy (C}_4\text{ plants)}
description: Links anatomy to C4 photosynthesis. Vascular bundles surrounded by a sheath of large thick-walled chloroplast-rich bundle-sheath cells = Kranz anatomy of C4 grasses (e.g., maize, sugarcane).

subject: Biology
title: Lung Volumes
description: TV (Tidal Vol) = 500ml. IRV (Inspiratory Reserve) = 2500-3000ml. ERV (Expiratory Reserve) = 1000-1100ml. RV (Residual) = 1100-1200ml.

subject: Biology
title: Respiratory Capacities
description: Derived volumes. Vital Capacity (VC) is max air breathed out after forced inspiration. FRC is air remaining after normal expiration.
derivation: TLC = VC + RV (Total Lung Capacity).

subject: Biology
title: Regulation of Respiration
description: Respiratory Rhythm Centre (Medulla). Pneumotaxic Centre (Pons) - reduces duration of inspiration. Chemosensitive Area - sensitive to CO2 and H+.
visual_data: \text{High } CO_2/H^+ \to \text{Signal to Rhythm Centre} \to \text{Increase Breathing Rate}

subject: Biology
title: Transport of Gases
description: O2: 97% by RBC (Oxyhaemoglobin), 3% dissolved in plasma. CO2: 70% as Bicarbonate (HCO3-), 20-25% as Carbamino-Hb, 7% dissolved.
visual_data: CO_2 + H_2O \xrightarrow{\text{Carbonic Anhydrase}} H_2CO_3 \to HCO_3^- + H^+

subject: Biology
title: Standard Lung Volumes
description: Standard reference values of the four primary respiratory volumes in a healthy adult human. \(TV\)=tidal volume, \(IRV\)=inspiratory reserve volume, \(ERV\)=expiratory reserve volume, \(RV\)=residual volume.

subject: Biology
title: O2 Transport in Blood
description: Distribution of oxygen carried by blood. About 97% binds reversibly with haemoglobin as oxyhaemoglobin; only ~3% is dissolved in plasma.

subject: Biology
title: O2 Binding & Delivery
description: Each haemoglobin molecule binds 4 O2 molecules; ~5 mL O2 is delivered to tissues by every 100 mL of oxygenated blood under normal conditions.

subject: Biology
title: CO2 Delivery to Alveoli
description: About 4 mL of CO2 is delivered to the alveoli by every 100 mL of deoxygenated blood under normal physiological conditions.

subject: Biology
title: Partial Pressures (O2 & CO2)
visual_data: \begin{aligned} & \text{Alveoli: } pO_2 = 104,\ pCO_2 = 40 \\ & \text{Deoxy. blood: } pO_2 = 40,\ pCO_2 = 45 \\ & \text{Oxy. blood: } pO_2 = 95,\ pCO_2 = 40 \\ & \text{Tissues: } pO_2 = 40,\ pCO_2 = 45 \end{aligned}
description: Standard partial pressures (in mmHg) of O2 and CO2 at exchange sites; gases diffuse down these gradients. \(pO_2\)=partial pressure of oxygen, \(pCO_2\)=partial pressure of carbon dioxide.

subject: Biology
title: Atmospheric vs Alveolar pO2/pCO2
description: Partial pressures (in mmHg) of respiratory gases in atmospheric air versus alveolar air; drop in \(pO_2\) and rise in \(pCO_2\) drives diffusion at the alveoli.

subject: Biology
title: Protein Digestion Sequence
description: Sequential breakdown of proteins. Pepsin requires acidic pH (1.8). Trypsin/Chymotrypsin require alkaline pH (7.8) activated by Enterokinase.
derivation: Protein $\to$ Proteoses/Peptones $\to$ Dipeptides $\to$ Amino Acids.

subject: Biology
title: Human Dental Formula
description: Arrangement of teeth in each half of upper and lower jaw: Incisors (2), Canines (1), Premolars (2), Molars (3). Thecodont, Diphyodont, Heterodont.
derivation: Child Formula: 2102/2102 (20 teeth). No Premolars in milk teeth.

subject: Biology
title: Liver & Bile
description: Largest gland. Hepatic lobules (structural unit). Secretes Bile (No enzymes, emulsifies fats). Bile stored in Gall Bladder.

subject: Biology
title: Absorption Mechanisms
description: Simple Diffusion (Small amts of Glucose, Amino acids, Cl-). Facilitated Transport (Glucose, AA with carrier Na+). Active Transport (Against gradient - Na+).

subject: Biology
title: Rennin (Infant Stomach)
description: Milk-clotting enzyme active in infants; coagulates soluble milk protein. \(Ca^{2+}\)=calcium ions required for curdling.

subject: Biology
title: Nucleic Acid Digestion
description: Pancreatic and intestinal breakdown of DNA/RNA to nitrogenous bases and pentose sugars. Nucleases act in duodenum, nucleotidases/nucleosidases at brush border.

subject: Biology
title: Bile Composition & Function
description: Hepatic secretion aiding fat emulsification; contains no digestive enzymes. Bile salts emulsify fats, bile pigments are Hb breakdown waste.

subject: Biology
title: Absorptive Surface Amplification
description: Structural adaptations that maximise nutrient absorption in small intestine. Villi (finger-like folds) bear microvilli, each villus has a capillary network and a lacteal.

subject: Biology
title: Vitamin & Water Absorption Routes
visual_data: \text{Fat-soluble (A, D, E, K) + Fats} \to \text{Lymph} \quad ; \quad \text{Glucose, Amino acids, Water-soluble vitamins} \to \text{Blood}
description: Differential routing of absorbed nutrients. Fats and fat-soluble vitamins enter lacteals (lymph); water-soluble nutrients enter intestinal capillaries (blood).

subject: Biology
title: Site-wise Absorption Summary
visual_data: \text{Mouth/Stomach: minimal} \quad \to \quad \text{Small Intestine: maximum} \quad \to \quad \text{Large Intestine: water + minerals}
description: Region-wise absorption intensity in the gut. Small intestine is principal absorptive site; large intestine reabsorbs water, some minerals and drugs.

subject: Biology
topic: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
title: Animal Breeding
description: Inbreeding (Same breed - increases homozygosity/pure line, but inbreeding depression). Outcrossing (Same breed, no common ancestor). Cross-breeding (Different breeds - Hisardale sheep).
visual_data:
MOET: Multiple Ovulation Embryo Transfer
Cow -> FSH -> 6-8 eggs -> AI -> Embryo recovery -> Surrogate

subject: Biology
topic: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
title: Green Revolution Varieties
description: Wheat: Sonalika, Kalyan Sona (Norman Borlaug). Rice: Jaya, Ratna (IR-8). Sugarcane: Saccharum barberi (North) x S. officinarum (South).
visual_data:
Biofortification: Breeding for higher nutrient content
Example: Atlas 66 (Wheat - High Protein), Iron-fortified Rice

subject: Biology
topic: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
title: Single Cell Protein (SCP)
description: Alternative protein source for humans/animals. Spirulina (Blue-green algae), Methylophilus methylotrophus (Bacteria - high rate of biomass production).

subject: Biology
topic: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
title: Biofortification Examples
description: Breeding crops with higher vitamins/minerals. Vitamin A enriched Carrots/Spinach. Vitamin C enriched Bitter gourd. Iron enriched Rice.

subject: Biology
topic: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
title: Honey Bee Colony
description: Composition of a honeybee (Apis) colony for apiculture. One fertile queen, a few male drones, and thousands of sterile female worker bees per hive.

subject: Biology
topic: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
title: Tissue Culture Yield
description: Capacity of plant tissue culture. A single explant (any plant part) grown on nutrient medium under aseptic conditions can produce thousands of genetically identical plants (somaclones).

subject: Biology
topic: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
title: Spirulina Biomass
visual_data: \text{Spirulina} \to \text{rich in Protein, Minerals, Fats, Carbohydrate, Vitamins}
description: Spirulina as Single Cell Protein (SCP). Grown on waste materials (e.g. molasses, sewage), it yields large biomass that is a rich nutritional supplement, reducing pressure on food/feed protein.

subject: Biology
topic: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
title: Saccharum Sugarcane Cross
visual_data: Saccharum\ barberi\ (\text{N.India}) \times Saccharum\ officinarum\ (\text{S.India}) \to \text{high yield + high sugar + thick stem}
description: Classic plant breeding success crossing North-Indian Saccharum barberi (low sugar, thin) with tropical Saccharum officinarum (high sugar, thick) to give superior canes that thrive in North India.

subject: Biology
topic: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
title: Somatic Hybridization
description: Fusion of naked protoplasts (cell-wall removed by enzymes) of two different varieties to make a hybrid without sexual crossing; e.g. Pomato from potato + tomato protoplasts.

subject: Biology
title: Famous Scientists & Discoveries
description: Schleiden & Schwann (Cell Theory). Rudolf Virchow (Omnis cellula-e cellula). Singer & Nicolson (Fluid Mosaic). Watson & Crick (DNA Double Helix).
visual_data:
Mendel: Father of Genetics
Morgan: Linkage (Fruit fly)
Sutton & Boveri: Chromosomal Theory
Darwin: Natural Selection

subject: Biology
title: Taxonomic Hierarchy
description: Arrangement of categories. Species (Basic unit) -> Genus -> Family -> Order -> Class -> Phylum/Division -> Kingdom.
visual_data:
Mnemonic: 'Keep Pot Clean Or Family Gets Sick'
Potato: Solanum tuberosum
Human: Homo sapiens (Order: Primata, Class: Mammalia)

subject: Biology
title: Binomial Nomenclature
description: Carolus Linnaeus. Two components: Generic name (Capitalized) + Specific epithet (Lower case). Latinized and written in Italics (or underlined).
visual_data:
Example: Mangifera indica (Mango)
Author citation: Mangifera indica Linn.

subject: Biology
title: Taxonomic Aids
description: Herbarium (Dried plant sheets). Botanical Gardens (Living plants - Kew, NBRI). Museum (Preserved specimens). Zoological Parks (Wild animals).
visual_data:
Key: Analytical device (Couplet of contrasting characters)
Flora: Index of plants in a given area

subject: Biology
title: Defining Properties of Life
description: Metabolism (Sum of all chemical reactions) and Consciousness (Response to stimuli) are defining properties. Growth and Reproduction are NOT defining (exceptions exist).

subject: Biology
title: Taxon Categories Count
description: Number and order of obligatory taxonomic categories from highest to lowest. As we go down (Kingdom to Species): number of common characters increases, while number of organisms in the taxon decreases. \(7\)=obligate categories.

subject: Biology
title: Characters vs Hierarchy Rule
visual_data: \text{Higher category} \rightarrow \text{Common characters} \downarrow \\ \text{Higher category} \rightarrow \text{Number of organisms} \uparrow \\ \text{(Lower category} \rightarrow \text{reverse)}
description: Inverse relation used in NEET reasoning MCQs on taxonomic hierarchy. Going from species up to kingdom, shared characters decrease and member count increases.

subject: Biology
title: Species Diversity (Known)
description: Standard NCERT figure for the number of species so far described and identified on Earth (out of an estimated far larger total). Frequently asked numerical recall.

subject: Biology
title: Metabolism Defining Rule
description: Defining property: all living organisms show metabolism (sum of all chemical reactions). Isolated metabolic reactions in a test tube are living reactions but not 'living'. Common assertion-reason MCQ.

subject: Biology
title: Consciousness — Defining Property
visual_data: \text{Consciousness} = \text{Defining property of living} \\ \text{(Sense + respond to environmental stimuli)}
description: NCERT-stated 'most obvious and technically complicated' defining feature of living organisms; all organisms respond to stimuli (light, water, temperature, etc.). Human is the only self-conscious organism.

subject: Biology
title: ICBN vs ICZN Codes
description: Standardised codes agreed by biologists for naming. ICBN = International Code for Botanical Nomenclature (plants); ICZN = International Code of Zoological Nomenclature (animals).

subject: Biology
title: Binomial Name — Rules
description: Universal rules of binomial nomenclature (given by Carolus Linnaeus). Genus name starts with capital letter, species name in lowercase; both italicised in print or separately underlined when handwritten.
